beginner.content:
1. Definition

• href stands for Hypertext REFerence.
• It holds the destination of the link.
• It is the most important attribute of the <a> tag.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To tell the browser where to go when the link is clicked.
• Without href, the anchor is just decorated text - nothing happens on click.

3. Need of This Topic

• href accepts many different kinds of value: a web page, an email, a phone number, a file, a section of the same page.
• Knowing which form to use is essential for building any real website.
• A wrong href is the single most common cause of a broken link.
codeExamples:

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Very flexible - one attribute handles web pages, files, email, phone and page sections.
• Simple to write - just the address in quotes.
• Copyable - the user can right-click and copy the link address.
• Visible before clicking - the browser shows the destination in the status bar, so users can check it is safe.

5. Disadvantages

• Typing mistakes break it silently - there is no error message, just a 404 page.
• Case sensitive on Linux servers - About.html and about.html are different files.
• Spaces break URLs - they must be written as %20.
• href="#" is misused for buttons, which jumps the page to the top.
• Relative paths break when a file is moved to a different folder.

• Flipkart - each product link is href="/product/item-id".
• College websites - href to a PDF so students can download the syllabus.
• Restaurant sites - href="tel:..." so a phone user taps once to call.
• Support pages - href="mailto:..." to open the email app pre-filled.
• Long articles - href="#section" to build a table of contents.

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• href holds a URL, which may be absolute, relative, or a special scheme such as mailto:, tel:, sms: or javascript:.
• The browser resolves a relative href against the document's base URL to produce the final absolute URL.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To express a resource location that survives being copied, bookmarked and shared.
• Because it is resolved at click time, a relative href automatically follows the site to a new domain.

3. Need (Advanced)

• URL encoding rules matter as soon as you build links from data.
• Query values containing &, spaces or Hindi text must be encoded, or the link breaks or is misread.
• Building links by string concatenation is the source of countless bugs and of injection vulnerabilities.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Protocol relative resolution - a root relative href works on localhost, staging and production without change.
• The URL API gives safe, correct encoding with no manual escaping.
• Special schemes integrate the page with the device: dialer, email client, SMS, maps.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• javascript: URLs are a security hole - they are a direct XSS vector and are blocked by most Content Security Policies.
• Never put user input into href unchecked - a value of javascript:alert(1) becomes executable code.
• & must be written as & in the HTML source to be valid.
• The <base> tag silently changes every relative link on the page, including ones you did not intend.
• Very long URLs can be truncated by some email clients and servers.
codeExamples: Search (valid)

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Twitter and Facebook - rewrite every user posted href through a redirect service to scan it for malware before the user arrives.
• Google Analytics - appends utm_source and utm_campaign parameters to href so marketing traffic can be traced.
• WhatsApp share buttons - build href="https://wa.me/?text=..." with the message URL-encoded.
• Payment gateways - never place the amount in the href, because a user can edit it. The amount is validated on the server.
• Content Security Policy - production sites block javascript: URLs entirely at the browser level.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The target attribute decides where the linked page opens.
• It is written on the <a> tag alongside href.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To control whether the page replaces the current tab or opens a new one.
• To keep the user on your site while still letting them view an external page.

3. Need of This Topic

• Sending a user away from a half-filled form loses their work.
• Opening every link in a new tab, however, floods the browser with tabs and breaks the Back button expectation.
• Choosing correctly is a real user-experience decision.

The Four Values

• _self - same tab. This is the default.
• _blank - a new tab or window.
• _parent - the parent frame.
• _top - the full window, breaking out of all frames.
codeExamples:

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Keeps your site open - the user does not lose their place.
• Protects unsaved work - a half-completed form is not destroyed.
• Good for reference links - documentation opened beside the tutorial.
• Good inside web apps - a help page opens without losing app state.

5. Disadvantages

• Breaks the Back button - in a new tab there is no history to go back to. This confuses many users.
• Tab clutter - twenty links means twenty tabs.
• Security risk - without rel="noopener" the new page can control your tab.
• Accessibility problem - a screen reader user may not realise a new tab opened and gets lost.
• Takes away user choice - users who want a new tab already know Ctrl+click.
• Bad on mobile - tab switching on a phone is awkward.
codeExamples:

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Online exam portals - instructions open in a new tab so the exam timer is not lost.
• Banking sites - a third-party link opens in a new tab so your session stays alive.
• Government websites - external links open new tabs and show a notice that you are leaving the site.
• Documentation sites - code sandbox examples open separately.
• Job portals - the company website opens in a new tab so your application form is preserved.
codeExamples:

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• target names a browsing context - a tab, window or frame.
• Besides the four keywords, any custom name can be used. The first click creates that context; later clicks with the same name reuse it.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To direct navigation into a specific context rather than always creating a new one.
• A named target lets several links share one secondary window instead of opening many.

3. Need (Advanced)

• Without a named target, ten reference links create ten tabs.
• With a shared name they all reuse a single tab - the behaviour documentation sites want.
• Understanding contexts also explains why _top and _parent exist, and why iframes need them.

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Named contexts prevent tab explosion in documentation and admin tools.
• _top lets a page break out of a hostile frame, part of clickjacking defence.
• Iframe targeting allows a classic preview pane with no JavaScript at all.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Reverse tabnabbing - the opened page receives a window.opener reference and can set window.opener.location, silently replacing your tab with a fake login page. The user then sees a trusted-looking tab they never navigated away from.
• Modern browsers imply noopener for target="_blank", but older browsers and some in-app webviews do not.
• noreferrer also hides analytics - the destination no longer knows the traffic came from you, which may matter for partners.
• Popup blockers can block programmatic window.open, though not a genuine user click.
codeExamples: Safe Safest

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• GitHub - every user-supplied link in a README gets rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" added server side.
• Online IDEs - the preview pane is an iframe, and Run targets that named frame.
• Banking portals - use _top plus frame-busting so their pages cannot be embedded in an attacker's frame.
• Admin dashboards - reports open into one named "reportWindow" so staff are not buried in tabs.
• Email clients - force target="_blank" with noreferrer on every link so the mailbox session is never exposed.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• rel stands for relationship.
• It describes how the linked page relates to the current page.
• It does not change what the link does - it adds information about the link.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To tell browsers and search engines how to treat this link.
• To make links safe when they open in a new tab.
• To control whether your site's SEO reputation is passed to the destination.

3. Need of This Topic

• Without rel="noopener", a target="_blank" link is a real security hole.
• Without rel="nofollow", spam and paid links can damage your search ranking.
• Google may penalise a site that passes ranking to paid links.

Common Values

• noopener - the new page cannot control your tab.
• noreferrer - do not tell the destination where the user came from.
• nofollow - do not pass SEO ranking.
• sponsored - this is a paid or advertising link.
• ugc - user generated content, such as a comment.
codeExamples:
External site
Safe new tab
Advertisement
Comment author
All three

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Security - noopener closes a genuine attack route in one word.
• SEO protection - nofollow stops spammers benefiting from your links.
• Privacy - noreferrer keeps your page URL private.
• Costs nothing - it is just an attribute, no performance impact.
• Clear intent - sponsored and ugc tell search engines exactly what kind of link this is.

5. Disadvantages

• Easy to forget - and forgetting it is a security bug, not a cosmetic one.
• noreferrer breaks analytics - your partner can no longer see that the traffic came from you.
• nofollow is only a hint - Google treats it as a hint, not a command.
• Overusing nofollow on your own internal links wastes ranking.
• Not validated - a typo such as rel="noopner" fails silently with no warning.
codeExamples: Protected Partner still sees the referral Courses

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Blog comment sections - WordPress adds rel="nofollow ugc" to every link a commenter posts, to stop comment spam.
• News websites - rel="sponsored" on advertiser links, as Google requires.
• Wikipedia - every external link carries rel="nofollow", which is why link spamming Wikipedia gives no SEO benefit.
• Email clients - rel="noreferrer" so the mailbox URL never leaks.
• Affiliate marketing sites - rel="sponsored nofollow" on every affiliate link, to stay within Google's rules.

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• rel holds a space separated list of link types defined by the HTML specification and the IANA link relation registry.
• On <a> it describes the relationship to a destination. On <link> in the head it declares resources such as stylesheet, icon, canonical and preload.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To let machines - crawlers, browsers, feed readers - understand link intent without parsing the page content.
• To control the browser's security and privacy behaviour on navigation.

3. Need (Advanced)

• Google replaced the single nofollow signal with three: nofollow, sponsored and ugc.
• Since 2020 these are hints, so Google may still choose to follow them.
• Getting them wrong on an affiliate site risks a manual penalty.
codeExamples: Next lesson Previous lesson Licence About the author My profile Paid link User posted link Untrusted link

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• noopener has zero cost and also improves performance: the new page runs in a separate process instead of sharing yours.
• Granular SEO signals - sponsored and ugc tell Google precisely why a link is untrusted.
• Referrer control can be tuned per link, more precisely than a page-wide policy.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• noreferrer removes the Referer header entirely, so partner attribution, affiliate tracking and fraud checks all break.
• A Referrer-Policy header is usually the better tool: it can send only the origin, keeping attribution while hiding the path.
• rel is not validated by browsers - unknown values are ignored silently.
• Blanket nofollow on all external links is now considered poor practice; it makes your site look like a dead end to crawlers.

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Google Search Console - flags affiliate links missing rel="sponsored" as a policy issue.
• Stack Overflow - adds rel="nofollow noreferrer" to links in answers from low-reputation users, and removes nofollow as reputation grows.
• Medium and Substack - apply rel="noopener nofollow ugc" to every author-inserted external link.
• Enterprise intranets - use rel="noreferrer" so internal URLs, which often contain employee ids, never reach the public internet.
• WordPress core - since version 4.7 it automatically injects noopener into any link the editor sets to open in a new tab.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The download attribute tells the browser to save the linked file instead of opening it.
• It is a boolean-style attribute, but it can also be given a value.
• That value becomes the suggested file name.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To force a download rather than displaying the file in the browser.
• To give the saved file a friendly, meaningful name.

3. Need of This Topic

• A PDF normally opens in the browser instead of downloading.
• Server files often have ugly names such as doc_8f2a91.pdf.
• The download attribute solves both problems with no server configuration.
codeExamples:
Opens in the browser
Downloads the file
Download Syllabus
Download Certificate

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• No server setup needed - one attribute replaces Content-Disposition headers.
• Friendly file names - the user gets Java-Syllabus.pdf, not doc_8f2a91.pdf.
• Predictable behaviour - the user knows a file is being saved.
• Works with generated files - blob and data URLs can be downloaded too.

5. Disadvantages

• Same-origin only - on a cross-origin file the rename is ignored, and in modern browsers the download attribute itself is ignored.
• The user can still rename it - it is only a suggestion.
• Not supported in very old browsers - they simply open the file.
• Mobile behaviour varies - some in-app browsers ignore it entirely.
• No progress indication for large files beyond the browser's own UI.
• Security filtering - browsers may block dangerous extensions such as .exe.
codeExamples:
Download report
Download Notes (PDF, 2 MB)

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• JavaSchoolLab certificates - the certificate is generated in the browser and downloaded as a PDF.
• Bank statements - download as PDF with a name like Statement-Sep-2025.pdf.
• College portals - download the hall ticket or admit card.
• E-commerce - download the invoice for an order.
• Data dashboards - export a table as a CSV file created entirely in the browser.
codeExamples:
Student Portal

Download Hall Ticket

Export marks as CSV

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• download instructs the browser to treat the resource as an attachment rather than navigating to it.
• It is subject to the same-origin policy: for a cross-origin URL it is ignored unless the server opts in.
• The file name is sanitised by the browser - path separators are stripped, so download="../../etc/passwd" cannot escape the downloads folder.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To let the client control file delivery without a server round trip or a Content-Disposition header.
• To make client-generated files - CSV, JSON, PDF, canvas images - saveable.

3. Need (Advanced)

• Generating a report on the client avoids server load entirely.
• Data that must never leave the browser for privacy reasons can still be exported.
• Object URLs must be revoked or the memory leaks for the life of the page.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Zero server cost - export features need no backend endpoint at all.
• Privacy - sensitive data can be exported without ever being uploaded.
• Works offline - a service worker plus client generation means downloads still work with no network.
• Safe by design - the browser strips path characters from the file name.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Memory - a large blob lives entirely in RAM. Generating a 500 MB CSV will crash the tab.
• No resume - a failed blob download cannot be resumed the way a server download can.
• Cross-origin blocked - since Chrome 65 the attribute is ignored for cross-origin URLs, to prevent a site tricking users into saving files from elsewhere under a misleading name.
• Sandboxed iframes block downloads unless allow-downloads is set.
• Browser safe browsing may warn on or block certain file types.
• Data URLs over a few megabytes are blocked in most browsers - use a blob instead.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>Large file downloads</title></head>
<body>

  <button onclick="badWay()">Naive (memory heavy)</button>
  <button onclick="goodWay()">Streamed (memory safe)</button>

  <script>
    // DISADVANTAGE: everything held in memory at once.
    // For a very large export this crashes the tab.
    function badWay() {
      var rows = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 200000; i++) {
        rows.push(i + ",Student " + i + "," + (i % 100));
      }
      var blob = new Blob([rows.join("\n")], { type: "text/csv" });
      console.log("blob size:", (blob.size / 1048576).toFixed(1), "MB");
      // A 500 MB build would fail here
    }

    // BETTER: build in chunks so peak memory stays lower
    function goodWay() {
      var parts = [];
      var chunk = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 200000; i++) {
        chunk.push(i + ",Student " + i + "," + (i % 100));
        if (chunk.length === 5000) {
          parts.push(chunk.join("\n") + "\n");
          chunk = [];                 // release each chunk
        }
      }
      if (chunk.length) parts.push(chunk.join("\n"));

      // Blob accepts an ARRAY of parts - no giant single string
      var blob = new Blob(parts, { type: "text/csv" });
      console.log("blob size:", (blob.size / 1048576).toFixed(1), "MB");

      // For genuinely huge exports, stream from the SERVER instead:
      //   Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="export.csv"
      //   Transfer-Encoding: chunked
    }
  </script>

  <!-- Downloads inside a sandboxed iframe need explicit permission -->
  <!-- <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-downloads"></iframe> -->

</body>
</html>

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Google Sheets - Download as CSV builds the file in the browser for small sheets, and streams from the server for large ones.
• GitHub - Download ZIP is server generated, because the archive is too large to build client side.
• Banking portals - statements are always server generated and signed, so the PDF cannot be forged.
• JavaSchoolLab certificates - jsPDF builds the certificate in the browser, so no server rendering is needed.
• Analytics dashboards - export the visible chart as PNG from a canvas.
codeExamples:
Decision guide

Small file, no secrets, no signing needed
    -> build in the browser with Blob + download
       (CSV export, chart PNG, JSON settings)

Large file, or must be authoritative/signed
    -> generate on the SERVER and send
       Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="x.pdf"
       (bank statements, invoices, ZIP archives)

Cross-origin file
    -> the download attribute is IGNORED.
       Proxy it through your own domain, or set the
       header on the origin server.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• An absolute URL is the complete address of a page or file.
• It includes the protocol, the domain name and the full path.
• Example: https://javaschoollab.com/courses/java.html

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To point at a resource anywhere on the internet.
• To give an address that works no matter which page it is written on.

3. Need of This Topic

• To link to another website, an absolute URL is the only option.
• Emails, RSS feeds and sitemaps must use absolute URLs, because there is no page to be relative to.
• Social sharing tags require the full address.
codeExamples: Java Course Google Oracle Java Tutorial

beginner.content:
4. Syntax and Parts of an Absolute URL

• Full form: protocol://subdomain.domain.tld:port/path?query#fragment

The Parts Explained

• protocol - https:// or http://. Always use https.
• subdomain - www, blog, shop. Optional.
• domain - javaschoollab.
• tld - .com, .in, .org.
• port - :8080. Optional, defaults to 443 for https.
• path - /courses/java.html.
• query - ?level=basic&sort=new. Extra data.
• fragment - #section2. Jumps to a part of the page.
codeExamples:
https://shop.javaschoollab.com:8080/courses/java?level=basic#syllabus
-----   ----------------------- ---- ------------ ----------- --------
  |               |              |        |            |         |
protocol       host+subdomain   port    path        query    fragment
Courses Search Syllabus Local dev server

beginner.content:
5. Advantages

• Works from anywhere - the same URL is valid on any page, in any email, in any app.
• Only way to reach another site.
• Unambiguous - there is no guessing about which folder you are in.
• Safe when content moves - if a page is copied into an email or RSS feed, the link still works.
• Required for SEO tags - canonical and Open Graph tags must be absolute.

6. Disadvantages

• Breaks when the domain changes - moving from example.com to example.in means editing every link.
• Painful across environments - a hard-coded https://mysite.com does not work on localhost or staging.
• Longer to type and more error prone.
• Mixed content errors - an http:// resource on an https:// page is blocked by the browser.
• Larger file size - hundreds of long URLs add real bytes to a page.
codeExamples: About (works on every environment)

beginner.content:
7. Real Time Examples

• Email newsletters - every link must be absolute, because an email has no website to be relative to.
• Sitemap.xml - Google requires absolute URLs; this site's sitemap uses https://javaschoollab.com/... for all 2,238 entries.
• Social sharing - the og:url tag must be absolute or WhatsApp shows no preview.
• CDN assets - Bootstrap and Font Awesome are loaded from an absolute CDN URL.
• Payment gateways - the return URL sent to Razorpay must be absolute.
• QR codes - always encode an absolute URL.
codeExamples: View our courses | Unsubscribe

beginner.content:
8. Common Mistakes

• Forgetting https:// - href="google.com" looks for a folder named google.com inside your site.
• Using http instead of https - causes mixed content warnings.
• Hard-coding the domain for internal links, which breaks local testing.
• Spaces in the URL - must be encoded as %20.
• Wrong case in the path - fails on Linux servers.

9. Best Practices

• Use absolute URLs only for external sites, emails, sitemaps and meta tags.
• Use root-relative URLs such as /about for your own pages.
• Always write https.
• Store the base domain in one config value rather than repeating it.
• Add rel="noopener noreferrer" whenever the link opens in a new tab.
codeExamples:
MISTAKE 1: missing protocol

Google

MISTAKE 2: hard-coding your own domain

Contact

MISTAKE 3: spaces

File

BEST PRACTICE: one base value, reused

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• Formally, an absolute URL contains a scheme and enough information to be resolved with no base URL.
• A scheme-relative URL such as //cdn.example.com/x.js is a special case: it inherits the current page's protocol.
• A root-relative URL such as /about is not absolute - it still needs the current origin.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To identify a resource globally and unambiguously, independent of context.
• To be storable - in a database, an email, a QR code - and still resolve correctly years later.

3. Need (Advanced)

• The origin - scheme plus host plus port - drives CORS, cookies, localStorage and the same-origin policy.
• Two URLs differing only by http vs https are different origins, so they do not share storage or cookies.
• Understanding this is essential for debugging CORS and authentication failures.

4. Advanced Reference - URL Encoding Rules

• Different parts of a URL allow different characters.
• encodeURIComponent - for a single value such as a query parameter. Encodes / ? : @ & = + $ #
• encodeURI - for a whole URL. Leaves the structural characters alone.
• Never use encodeURI on a single parameter value - an ampersand inside it will not be encoded and will split the query.

Reserved vs Unreserved

• Unreserved - A to Z, a to z, 0 to 9, and - _ . ~ Safe everywhere.
• Reserved - : / ? # [ ] @ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; = They have structural meaning.
• A space becomes %20 in a path, and may be + in a query string.
• Punycode - non-English domains such as भारत.भारत are converted to an xn-- form.

5. Advantages (Advanced)

• Cacheable and shareable - a stable absolute URL can be cached by a CDN and shared safely.
• Content addressable - fingerprinted asset URLs such as app.a3f9c1.js allow year-long cache headers.
• Required by protocols - RSS, sitemaps, JSON-LD structured data and OAuth redirect URIs all demand absolute URLs.

6. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Environment coupling - hard-coded domains are the single biggest cause of staging leaks into production.
• Protocol downgrade - an http absolute URL on an https page is blocked, silently breaking images and scripts.
• Open redirect vulnerability - accepting an absolute URL from a query parameter and redirecting to it lets an attacker send users to a phishing site using your trusted domain in the link.
• SSRF risk on the server - fetching a user-supplied absolute URL can expose internal services.
• Scheme-relative URLs are now discouraged, because everything should simply be https.

7. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• OAuth and Google Sign-In - the redirect_uri must be an exact absolute URL registered in advance, precisely to stop open redirects.
• Razorpay and Stripe - callback URLs are absolute and whitelisted per merchant account.
• Cloudflare and Akamai - fingerprinted absolute asset URLs are cached for a year.
• Next.js and Vite - inject the base URL at build time, so no domain is ever hard-coded in source.
• JavaSchoolLab - VITE_API_BASE_URL is a build-time variable for exactly this reason.
• Password reset emails - contain an absolute URL with a single-use token, which is why noreferrer matters on those pages.

8. Interview Questions

• Q: What is the difference between an absolute and a relative URL?
A: An absolute URL contains the scheme and host and resolves with no context. A relative URL is resolved against the current document's base URL.

• Q: Is /about an absolute URL?
A: No. It is root-relative. It still needs the current origin to resolve. Only a URL with a scheme is absolute.

• Q: What is an origin?
A: Scheme plus host plus port. It determines the same-origin policy, cookies, storage and CORS.

• Q: Are http://site.com and https://site.com the same origin?
A: No. Different schemes mean different origins, so they do not share cookies or localStorage.

• Q: What is an open redirect and how do you prevent it?
A: Redirecting to a user-supplied URL. Prevent it by allowing only same-origin paths, never a full URL from input.

• Q: encodeURI or encodeURIComponent?
A: encodeURIComponent for a single value, encodeURI for a whole URL. Best of all, use the URL API.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• A relative URL gives the address relative to the current page.
• It has no protocol and no domain name.
• Example: about.html, images/logo.png, ../index.html

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To link between pages within your own website.
• To keep links short and easy to maintain.

3. Need of This Topic

• Writing the full domain on every internal link is repetitive and fragile.
• If the domain changes, every absolute link must be edited; relative links keep working.
• The same code then runs on localhost, staging and production with no change.
codeExamples:
About (same folder)
Java course (sub-folder)
Home (one folder up)
Contact

beginner.content:
4. Syntax - The Four Forms

• same folder - about.html or ./about.html
• sub-folder - courses/java.html
• parent folder - ../index.html
• root relative - /courses/java.html (starts from the site root)

The Symbols

• ./ - the current folder. Usually optional.
• ../ - go up one folder. Can be repeated: ../../
• / at the start - start from the website root, ignoring the current folder.
• no symbol - the current folder.
codeExamples:
Folder structure:

  website/
    |- index.html
    |- about.html
    |- images/
    |    |- logo.png
    |- courses/
         |- java.html
         |- python.html
         |- notes/
              |- unit1.html
Python course
Same thing, explicit
Unit 1 notes
About
Home

Home (root relative)

beginner.content:
5. Advantages

• Short and readable - less typing, fewer mistakes.
• Portable - the whole site can be moved to a new domain with no edits.
• Works offline - open the files directly from a folder and links still work.
• Environment independent - identical behaviour on localhost, staging and production.
• Smaller page size - hundreds of short links save real bytes.

6. Disadvantages

• Breaks when a file moves - a page moved into a sub-folder needs every ../ recounted.
• Confusing to count - deep folders lead to ../../../ which is easy to get wrong.
• Cannot leave your site - external links must be absolute.
• Fails in email - there is no base page, so relative links are meaningless.
• The <base> tag can silently change them all.
• Trailing slash matters - /courses and /courses/ resolve relative links differently.
codeExamples:
Page URL: /courses          (no trailing slash)
  href="java.html"  resolves to  /java.html        WRONG

Page URL: /courses/         (with trailing slash)
  href="java.html"  resolves to  /courses/java.html  correct

The browser treats the last segment as a FILE unless
the URL ends with a slash.
Always correct

beginner.content:
7. Real Time Examples

• Any multi-page website - the navigation menu uses /about, /courses, /contact.
• WordPress themes - asset paths are relative so the theme works on any domain.
• Static site generators - Jekyll and Hugo generate root-relative links.
• React and Vue apps - router paths such as /dashboard are root-relative.
• JavaSchoolLab - the sidebar links to /course/java and /course/spring-boot.
• Documentation sites - relative links let the docs be browsed offline from a zip file.
codeExamples:
Home Courses About Contact
  • Core Java
  • Spring Boot
  • HTML & CSS
Official Java Docs

beginner.content:
8. Common Mistakes

• Miscounting ../ - one too many or too few, giving a 404.
• Forgetting the leading slash - about.html and /about.html behave very differently.
• Wrong case - Images/Logo.png fails on a Linux server.
• Using a Windows backslash - images\logo.png is invalid; URLs always use forward slashes.
• Assuming a trailing slash that is not there.

9. Best Practices

• Prefer root-relative (/path) for everything inside your site - it never breaks when a file moves.
• Keep folder names lowercase with hyphens.
• Never use backslashes.
• Test on a real server, not just by double-clicking the file.
• Use a link checker before going live.
codeExamples:
MISTAKE 1: Windows backslash

MISTAKE 2: leading slash confusion

MISTAKE 3: counting ../ wrongly

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• A relative reference is resolved against a base URL using the algorithm in RFC 3986.
• The base is normally the document URL, but <base href> overrides it for the whole page.
• Resolution removes dot segments: a/b/../c becomes a/c.

2. Purpose (Advanced)

• To decouple content from deployment location, so the same build works at any origin or sub-path.

3. Need (Advanced)

• Single page applications served from a sub-path - for example /app/ on a shared domain - break entirely if paths assume the root.
• Build tools therefore expose a base option that rewrites asset URLs at build time.
• Knowing how resolution works is what lets you debug a blank page after deployment.

4. Advanced Reference - Resolution Rules

• Starts with a scheme - used as is, base ignored.
• Starts with // - inherits the base scheme only.
• Starts with / - inherits scheme, host and port; replaces the path.
• Starts with ? - keeps the path, replaces the query.
• Starts with # - keeps everything, replaces the fragment.
• Empty string - the current document, without the fragment.
• Anything else - resolved against the base's directory, meaning everything up to and including the last slash.

The Directory Rule

• This is the source of the trailing slash confusion.
• Base /courses has directory /, so java.html gives /java.html.
• Base /courses/ has directory /courses/, so java.html gives /courses/java.html.

5. Advantages (Advanced)

• Deployment flexibility - one build can be hosted at /, /app/ or on a CDN.
• Portable archives - documentation zipped and opened locally still works with document-relative links.
• Environment parity - no domain in the source means no staging URL can leak into production.

6. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• SPA routing conflict - with client-side routing the browser URL changes without a real folder existing. A document-relative asset then resolves against a route that is not a directory, and the asset 404s. This is the classic "works on the home page, breaks on a deep link" bug.
• <base> side effects - it also changes in-page fragment links, so href="#top" navigates to another page.
• Server rewrite mismatch - a server that adds or removes trailing slashes changes how every relative link resolves.
• Not usable in emails, feeds or JSON APIs.

7. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Vite and Webpack - the base or publicPath option rewrites every asset URL at build time, which is how one build serves both / and /app/.
• GitHub Pages - project sites live at /repo-name/, so base must be set or every asset 404s. This is the most common GitHub Pages complaint.
• Nginx - a try_files rule serves index.html for every route, which is what makes SPA deep links work at all.
• Documentation sites - MkDocs and Docusaurus generate relative links so the docs can be browsed from a local folder.
• JavaSchoolLab - BrowserRouter with routes such as /course/:courseId/:topicId is exactly the case that needs root-relative assets plus an Nginx fallback.
codeExamples:
1. VITE - deploying to a sub-path

   // vite.config.ts
   export default defineConfig({
     base: '/app/',        // assets become /app/assets/...
   })

   Root deployment  -> base: '/'          (the default)
   GitHub Pages     -> base: '/repo-name/'


2. NGINX - make SPA deep links work

   location / {
     root /usr/share/nginx/html;
     try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
   }

   Without try_files, opening
   https://javaschoollab.com/course/java/topic/loops
   directly returns 404, because no such FILE exists.
   try_files serves index.html and lets the router take over.


3. THE TRAILING SLASH decision - pick one and enforce it

   # redirect /courses/ to /courses
   rewrite ^/(.*)/$ /$1 permanent;

   Mixing both creates duplicate URLs, splits SEO ranking
   and changes how every relative link resolves.


4. BASE TAG - powerful but dangerous

   <base href="/app/">

   It also rewrites  href="#section"  into  /app/#section,
   so in-page anchors navigate away. Prefer build-time
   rewriting over the base tag.

expert.content:
8. Interview Questions

• Q: What is the difference between about.html and /about.html?
A: The first is document-relative, resolved against the current folder. The second is root-relative, always from the site root.

• Q: Why does my image work on the home page but break on a deep route?
A: The path is document-relative. On /course/java it resolves against /course/, not the root. Use a leading slash.

• Q: What does ../ mean, and what happens if you use too many?
A: It moves up one folder. Extra ones are clamped at the root, so the URL silently resolves to the wrong place instead of erroring.

• Q: How does a trailing slash change resolution?
A: Without it the last segment is treated as a file name and discarded, so relative links resolve one level higher.

• Q: When must you use absolute URLs?
A: External sites, emails, sitemaps, canonical and Open Graph tags, OAuth redirect URIs.

• Q: What does the <base> tag do and why is it risky?
A: It changes the base for every relative URL, including fragment links, which can break in-page anchors.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• An internal link is a link that points to another page inside the same website.
• It is written with the <a> tag and a relative URL, for example about.html or /courses/java.html
• The visitor never leaves your domain when the link is clicked.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To move the student from one page of the site to another, like Home to Courses to Contact.
• To build the navigation menu that every website needs.
• To connect related content so a reader can keep exploring.

3. Need of This Topic

• A website is not one page. Without internal links each page is an island.
• Typing the full domain on every link is repetitive and breaks when the domain changes.
• Search engines like Google follow internal links to discover and rank your pages.
codeExamples:
JavaSchoolLab

About Us
Home | Java Course | Fees in Rupees | Contact

Read the Spring Boot syllabus.

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Short and readable - href="/fees.html" instead of the whole domain.
• Portable - the same files run on localhost, on staging and on the live server.
• Fast - the browser stays on the same domain, so no new DNS lookup is needed.
• Good for SEO - Google crawls internal links and understands your site structure.
• Easy to rename the domain - nothing to edit inside the pages.

5. Disadvantages

• A wrong folder path gives a 404 Not Found, and the mistake is silent until someone clicks.
• Moving a file to another folder breaks every link that pointed to it.
• On Linux servers the path is case sensitive, so About.html and about.html are different files.
• Too many links on one page confuse the reader and dilute SEO value.
codeExamples:
Java Course
About
Java

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart - the Electronics, Fashion and Grocery links in the top bar are internal links.
• IRCTC - Book Ticket, PNR Status and Cancel Ticket all stay inside irctc.co.in
• A college portal - Attendance, Marks and Fee Receipt pages are joined by internal links.
• Wikipedia - the blue words inside an article that jump to another Wikipedia article.
• Amazon - the breadcrumb Home > Mobiles > Samsung is a chain of internal links.
codeExamples:
Sinhgad College Student Portal

Attendance | Marks | Fee Receipt | Time Table

Home > Departments > Computer Engineering

Total fees payable: Rs. 85,000 - Pay Now

expert.content:
1. Definition

• At the production level an internal link is a same origin navigation, where origin means scheme plus host plus port.
• The browser resolves the relative href against the document base, which is the current URL or the value of <base href>.
• In a single page app the same anchor is usually intercepted by the router, so no full page reload happens.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To create a crawlable link graph so search engines can find every page from the home page.
• To pass link equity, that is ranking value, from strong pages to deeper pages.
• To let the router and the browser history work correctly with the Back button.

3. Need of This Topic

• Pages that no internal link points to are called orphan pages and are almost never indexed.
• Deep pages should be reachable in three clicks or less from the home page.
• Using a button with JavaScript instead of an anchor destroys crawling, Back button and open in new tab.
codeExamples:
Reports
Spring Boot Course
Spring Boot Course

expert.content:
4. Advantages

• Crawl budget is used well, because a flat link structure lets a crawler reach every page quickly.
• Anchor text tells search engines what the target page is about, so descriptive text ranks better.
• Prefetch is possible - the browser can load an internal page before the click using rel="prefetch".
• A single change in the router or in a shared header component updates the menu on every page.

5. Disadvantages

• Broken internal links accumulate silently, so a link checker must run in the build pipeline.
• Trailing slash and case mismatches create duplicate URLs, which splits SEO value between them.
• Redirect chains from old URLs to new ones waste crawl budget and slow the first paint.
• Prefetching every link wastes mobile data for users on limited plans in India.

Interview Point

• Always ship a canonical tag and 301 redirects when you rename an internal URL.
codeExamples:
Java Collections Framework tutorial
Java

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart category pages link down to sub categories and up to the parent, forming a clean hierarchy.
• GitHub links every file in a repository tree with internal links, which is why code search works.
• Wikipedia is famous for dense internal linking, which is a large reason it ranks so well.
• Banking portals such as SBI use internal links guarded by a session, so an unauthenticated hit redirects to login.
• A Next.js or React project uses a Link component that still renders a real anchor underneath.
codeExamples:
Home > Electronics > Mobiles > Redmi Note 13

Redmi Note 13 - Rs. 17,999

Similar Mobiles

  • Realme 12
  • Samsung M14
My Orders

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• An external link points to a page on a different website.
• It always uses an absolute URL with the protocol and the domain, for example https://www.wikipedia.org
• Clicking it takes the visitor away from your domain.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To send the reader to a source, a reference or a partner site.
• To credit the place where the information came from.
• To connect your site to social media, documentation and payment gateways.

3. Need of This Topic

• No website can hold every piece of information, so it must point outward.
• Quoting a source without linking to it looks unreliable to a reader.
• Forgetting https:// turns the link into an internal file link and gives a 404.
codeExamples:
Wikipedia

Read the official docs at Oracle Java Documentation.

Flipkart

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Credibility - linking to Oracle docs or to a government site proves your claim.
• Useful to the reader - they get the deeper detail without you writing it.
• Partnerships - links to a payment gateway or a job portal add real value.
• Search engines reward pages that cite good outside sources.

5. Disadvantages

• You lose the visitor if the link opens in the same tab and they never come back.
• Link rot - the other site can delete the page any day and your link becomes a 404.
• Security - without rel="noopener" the new tab can control your page through window.opener.
• Spam risk - linking to low quality sites can hurt your own search ranking.

The Safe Pattern

• target="_blank" opens a new tab, and rel="noopener noreferrer" makes it safe.
codeExamples:
Wikipedia (opens in a new tab)
Link posted by a user

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• A college website links to the AICTE and the university site for approvals.
• Flipkart links out to a payment gateway such as Razorpay during checkout.
• News sites like The Hindu link to the original PDF of a government order.
• GitHub README files link to the project home page and to the CI build badge.
• Almost every site has footer links to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube.
codeExamples:
Approved by AICTE and affiliated to SPPU.

Follow us: LinkedIn | YouTube

Contact the office

expert.content:
1. Definition

• An external link is a cross origin navigation, so the browser applies a different security context to the destination.
• The rel attribute is a space separated token list that tells the browser and the crawler how to treat the link.
• Key tokens are noopener, noreferrer, nofollow, sponsored and ugc.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To control what the destination site learns about your page through the Referer header.
• To stop reverse tabnabbing, where the opened tab rewrites your original tab to a fake login page.
• To declare paid and user generated links correctly so that search guidelines are followed.

3. Need of This Topic

• Modern browsers imply noopener with target="_blank", but old browsers in use across India do not.
• Advertisement links without rel="sponsored" can bring a manual search penalty.
• A referrer policy leak can expose internal URLs with query parameters such as an order id.
codeExamples:
Partner offer
Sponsored: Java bootcamp
Posted by a student
No referrer sent

expert.content:
4. Advantages

• noopener puts the new tab in a separate browsing context group, so it cannot touch window.opener.
• noreferrer hides the source URL, useful when the path contains an order id or a token.
• Content Security Policy with form-action and frame-ancestors adds a second layer of protection.
• Outbound link tracking through an event listener gives real data on which partners actually convert.

5. Disadvantages

• noreferrer breaks affiliate tracking, because the partner cannot see who sent the traffic.
• target="_blank" is often bad accessibility, since a screen reader user is not warned about the new tab.
• Link rot on external URLs is unavoidable, so a scheduled crawler job is needed to find dead links.
• Every external domain adds a DNS lookup and a TLS handshake, which is slow on 4G in smaller cities.

Interview Point

• Explain reverse tabnabbing and why rel="noopener" fixes it.
codeExamples: RBI website (new tab)

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Razorpay and PayU checkout redirects from an Indian shopping site are external navigations.
• Wikipedia marks all outside references with rel="nofollow" so it is not a spam target.
• Stack Overflow adds rel="nofollow ugc" to links inside answers written by users.
• Amazon affiliate links use a tracking id in the query string, so noreferrer must not be used there.
• DigiLocker links from a college portal open in a new tab with the safe rel tokens.
codeExamples:
Order total: Rs. 4,999

Buy the recommended Java book on Amazon DigiLocker

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• An email link is an anchor whose href starts with mailto: followed by an email address.
• Example: <a href="mailto:info@javaschoollab.com">Email us</a>
• Clicking it opens the default mail app with the address already filled.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To let a visitor contact you in one click instead of copying the address by hand.
• To pre fill the subject and the body so the enquiry arrives in a useful shape.
• To place a support address on a contact page or in the footer.

3. Need of This Topic

• Typing an email address by hand causes spelling mistakes and lost enquiries.
• A plain text address is not clickable on a mobile phone.
• Support teams need the subject line to be consistent so tickets can be sorted.
codeExamples:
info@javaschoollab.com
Ask about the Java course

Write to us at info@javaschoollab.com

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• One click contact with no typing mistakes.
• Pre filled subject helps the support team route the mail automatically.
• cc and bcc can be added, so a copy reaches the manager as well.
• Works on a phone, where it opens Gmail or the default mail app directly.
• Needs no server code at all, unlike a contact form.

5. Disadvantages

• Spam bots scan pages for mailto and harvest the address.
• If the visitor uses only webmail with no default mail app configured, nothing happens on click.
• The visitor can edit everything, so a mailto is not a reliable structured form.
• There is no confirmation that the mail was really sent.
codeExamples:
Request a fee receipt
Mail both coordinators
Good

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• College websites put principal@college.edu.in in the footer as a mailto link.
• Flipkart seller support pages give a mailto with a pre filled subject such as Order Issue.
• GitHub shows a mailto link for security disclosures on many open source projects.
• A job posting gives careers@company.com with the subject set to the role name.
• Bank branches list a branch manager email for grievance redressal.
codeExamples:
Careers at DHIPAN Software Tech

Apply for Java Developer: careers@dhipan.in

Grievance: grievance@dhipan.in

Call us | Email us

expert.content:
1. Definition

• mailto is a URI scheme defined by RFC 6068, not an HTML feature, so the operating system decides which app handles it.
• The part after the question mark is a set of hfields, and every value must be percent encoded.
• Supported hfields in practice are subject, body, cc and bcc. Others are usually ignored by mail clients.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To hand a structured draft to the user without running any server side mail code.
• To act as a fallback when a contact form API is down.
• To register a web mail client as the protocol handler using registerProtocolHandler.

3. Need of This Topic

• Enterprise support desks parse the subject line to create a ticket, so the format must be exact.
• Address harvesting bots are real, so the address usually must be obfuscated or assembled by script.
• Some clients cap the total mailto length near 2000 characters, so long bodies get truncated.
codeExamples: Contact support

expert.content:
4. Advantages

• Zero backend, so there is no SMTP server, no queue and no cost.
• The mail is sent from the user's own account, which means it lands in their Sent folder as proof.
• No CAPTCHA is needed, because there is no endpoint for a bot to abuse.
• Deep linking with a ticket reference makes automated triage possible.

5. Disadvantages

• No delivery guarantee and no analytics, so you cannot measure the conversion rate.
• On a desktop with no configured client the click does nothing, which looks like a broken site.
• Header injection is possible if user input is placed into the mailto without encoding, so always encode.
• Harvesting means an unprotected address will start receiving spam within days.

Interview Point

• A production contact page offers a real form as the primary path and mailto as the fallback.
codeExamples: Our server is busy. Email us instead

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Jira and Zendesk style desks create a ticket from the subject prefix, so the mailto sets it.
• Open source security policies publish security@project.org as the only accepted disclosure path.
• Indian government portals list a Public Information Officer email for RTI requests.
• SaaS invoices include a mailto with the invoice number in the subject for billing queries.
• Newsletters include an unsubscribe mailto as a required alternative to the web link.
codeExamples:

1. Definition

• A telephone link is an anchor whose href starts with tel: followed by a phone number.
• Example: <a href="tel:+919876543210">Call us</a>
• On a mobile phone it opens the dialer with the number already typed.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To let a mobile visitor call your office with a single tap.
• To make Call Now buttons work on a shop, clinic or coaching class website.
• To support click to call from a desktop app such as Skype or Teams.

3. Need of This Topic

• Most Indian traffic is on mobile, and users expect to tap a number and call.
• Copying a ten digit number by hand is slow and error prone.
• A plain printed number cannot be dialled directly from the browser.

beginner.content:

• No typing mistakes, since the number comes from the page.
• An extension can be added using a comma for a pause, for example tel:+912026543210,,101
• Works with desktop softphones such as Skype, Teams and many CRM diallers.

5. Disadvantages

• On a desktop with no calling app the click may do nothing at all.
• Without the country code the number fails for users roaming outside India.
• Spaces and dashes inside the href confuse some old dialers, so keep the href clean.
• Bots can scrape the number and use it for spam calls.

expert.content:
1. Definition

• tel is a URI scheme defined by RFC 3966 and the value should be in E.164 form, that is plus, country code and the national number.
• Sub address and extension are expressed with ;ext=101 or with commas that act as dial pauses.
• The operating system, not the browser, decides which application handles the scheme.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To make click to call measurable, since a call is often the highest value conversion for a business.
• To feed a CRM dialler or a WebRTC softphone from a web page.
• To let format detection be controlled instead of letting the browser guess.

3. Need of This Topic

• Safari on iOS auto links anything that looks like a number, which can wrongly turn a PIN code or an order id into a call link.
• Multi country products must render the correct dialling format per locale.
• Marketing needs per campaign tracking numbers, which means the number is dynamic.

4. Advantages

• Conversion tracking works, because a click event can be sent to analytics before the dialer opens.
• Dynamic number insertion ties an offline call back to the online campaign that produced it.
• Structured data with telephone in schema.org makes the number show directly in search results.
• A tel link plus a WhatsApp link covers almost every contact preference in the Indian market.

5. Disadvantages

• Desktop dead ends unless a handler is installed, so a visible number must always be printed too.
• Format detection differences between iOS and Android cause inconsistent rendering.
• Scraped numbers lead to spam calls, so obfuscation or a masked number service is often needed.
• A number stored without the country code cannot be reused for international users later.

Interview Point

• To build a table of contents at the top of a tutorial or a policy page.

3. Need of This Topic

1. Definition

• The fragment is the part of the URL after the hash and it is never sent to the server.
• The browser resolves it as an indicated part of the document, matching an id first and then a name on an anchor.
• :target is the CSS pseudo class that matches the element currently pointed to by the fragment.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To drive pure CSS interactions such as tabs and lightboxes with no JavaScript.
• To restore scroll position and focus for deep links shared over WhatsApp or email.
• To use text fragments, the newer syntax that highlights matching text without any id.

3. Need of This Topic

• Focus must move to the target, otherwise a keyboard user's next Tab starts from the top of the page again.
• A single page app must handle the hashchange event, because the router controls rendering.
• Content rendered after load means the browser jumps before the target exists, so the jump must be repeated.

expert.content:
4. Advantages

• No network cost, because the fragment never reaches the server.
• CSS only widgets such as tab panels using :target keep the JavaScript bundle small.
• Deep linking into documentation improves support quality, since a link points at one clause.
• Text fragments let you link into a page you do not control, which is very useful for citations.

5. Disadvantages

• The fragment is invisible to the server, so server side rendering cannot use it.
• Each :target change pushes a history entry, so the Back button behaviour can feel wrong.
• Lazy loaded or virtualised lists break the jump, because the target is not in the DOM yet.
• Analytics tools miss fragment only navigations unless hashchange is tracked explicitly.

Interview Point

• To create Back to Top and Skip to Content shortcuts.
• To mark important places in a long document so they can be reached in one click.

expert.content:
1. Definition

• A bookmark is the fragment target of a URL, resolved by the browser against the id attribute in the document.
• The id must be unique, must not contain a space, and is matched case sensitively in HTML5.
• The legacy anchor name attribute is obsolete in HTML5 and should not be produced by new code.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To create stable permalinks that documentation generators and search engines can rely on.
• To provide landmark navigation for assistive technology together with ARIA roles.
• To let a content pipeline generate slugs from headings automatically.

3. Need of This Topic

• An id is a public contract, so changing it breaks external links and must be treated as a breaking change.
• Generated slugs must be deduplicated, otherwise two headings with the same text collide.
• Focus management is required, since scrolling alone does not move keyboard focus in all browsers.

4. Advantages

• Stable permalinks let support teams and documentation cite an exact clause for years.
• Landmark plus skip link gives screen reader users a fast route past the navigation.
• Static site generators build the table of contents automatically from the heading ids.
• The pattern costs nothing at runtime, since it is only HTML attributes.

5. Disadvantages

• Id churn after a content edit silently breaks external links, so a redirect map may be needed.
• Ids are a global namespace in the document, so a widget can clash with page content.
• CSS selectors need escaping when an id starts with a digit or contains special characters.
• A skip link that is fully hidden with display none is skipped by the browser too, so it must be visually hidden instead.

Interview Point

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The <img> element puts a picture inside an HTML page.
• It is an empty element. It has no closing tag, so we never write </img>.
• It does not store the picture. It only stores the address of the picture in the src attribute.
• The browser reads that address, downloads the picture file, and draws it in the page.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To show product photos on shopping sites like Flipkart and Amazon.
• To show a student photo on a college portal profile page.
• To show logos, banners, icons and screenshots on any website.
• Text alone is boring. One good image explains a product faster than ten lines of text.

3. Need of This Topic

• Every real website you will build in your job has images, so this is a daily use tag.
• Without <img> you cannot show a mobile phone photo next to a price of Rs 14999.
• Interviewers ask this in the very first HTML round, so the basics must be perfect.
• All later topics such as alt, width, srcset and picture are built on top of <img>.

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Very simple. One line of HTML shows a picture, no extra code needed.
• Works everywhere. Every browser since 1993 supports <img>.
• Many formats. The same tag can show jpg, png, gif, webp and svg files.
• Style friendly. CSS can resize, round the corners or add a border to it.
• Accessible. The alt attribute lets a blind user hear what the picture shows.

5. Disadvantages

• Extra download. Each image is a separate network request, so pages get slow.
• Broken links. If the file path is wrong, the user sees an ugly broken icon.
• Layout shift. Without width and height the page jumps while the image loads.
• No text search. Text written inside a picture cannot be searched or copied.
• Data cost. A heavy 5 MB photo wastes mobile data of a village user on 3G.

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• <img> is a replaced element. Its box is filled by an external resource, so its size comes from the file and from CSS, not from child nodes.
• The parser creates the element and the preload scanner starts fetching src before the rest of the document is parsed.
• In the DOM it is an HTMLImageElement with properties like naturalWidth, complete, currentSrc and decode().
• It fires load and error events, which is what production error tracking hooks into.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To control Largest Contentful Paint, because on most e commerce pages the LCP element is an image.
• To remove Cumulative Layout Shift by reserving space using width, height and CSS aspect ratio.
• To decide loading strategy: eager plus fetchpriority high for the hero image and lazy for images below the fold.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Core Web Vitals are a ranking signal, so a badly coded <img> directly costs the business money.
• Accessibility audits and WCAG compliance fail when alt text is missing on informative images.
• Interview question: what is the difference between naturalWidth and width, and when is complete true.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Preload scanner friendly. A plain src in the HTML is discovered earlier than any image inserted by JavaScript.
• Native lazy loading. loading equal to lazy saves bandwidth with zero JavaScript and zero library.
• Priority hints. fetchpriority lets you win LCP without changing any image file.
• decode() promise. You can decode off the main thread and swap the image without jank.
• CDN friendly. The same tag can point to an image CDN url that resizes on the fly.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• No native art direction. A single <img> cannot change the crop per screen, you need <picture>.
• Lazy loading misuse on above the fold images makes LCP worse, a very common production bug.
• Hotlinking and CORS. Cross origin images taint a canvas unless crossorigin and CORS headers are set.
• Cache busting pain. Changing an image without changing the file name keeps old copies in CDN caches.
• Client hints support for automatic format switching is still not uniform across browsers.

6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Flipkart hero banner: eager plus fetchpriority high on the first banner, lazy on everything below, which cuts LCP by about a second on 4G.
• Amazon listing grid: the first row of product images is eager, the rest lazy, so a 60 image page downloads only 12 images at first.
• Wikipedia: serves thumbnails at exact requested widths from an image server instead of shrinking a huge original in the browser.
• GitHub avatars: served from a separate avatars domain with long cache headers and a size query parameter.
• College result portal: student photos loaded lazily in the marksheet list so a slow campus network is not flooded.
• Monitoring: a global error listener reports every broken product image to the logging server so the content team can fix the missing file.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• src means source. It tells the browser where the image file is kept.
• It is the only compulsory attribute of <img>. Without src there is nothing to show.
• The value can be a relative path like images/phone.jpg or a full url like https://cdn.site.com/phone.jpg.
• It can also be a data url, where the picture bytes are written directly inside the HTML.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To connect the page to the real picture file on the server.
• To let one page pull images from many places, for example a logo from your own folder and a product photo from a CDN.
• To change the picture later by only changing the src value.

3. Need of This Topic

• Most broken image problems for beginners come from a wrong src path, so this must be clear.
• You must know the difference between /images/a.jpg, images/a.jpg and ../images/a.jpg.
• In interviews they ask what happens when src is empty or missing.

4. Advantages

• Flexible. The same page can mix local files and remote CDN files.
• Easy to change. Update one src value and the whole page shows the new picture.
• Cache friendly. The browser stores the file by its src url and reuses it on the next page.
• Dynamic. JavaScript can change src to build sliders and image galleries.

5. Disadvantages

• Case sensitive on Linux servers. Phone.JPG and phone.jpg are different files, so it works on your Windows laptop but breaks on the server.
• Remote risk. If the other website deletes the file, your page shows a broken image.
• Hotlinking is stealing. Using someone else url uses their bandwidth and may be blocked.
• Data urls get big. A base64 image is about 33 percent larger and it cannot be cached separately.
• Space in file name breaks the path unless you write it as percent 20.

6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart: product photos come from a CDN url, while the site logo comes from a local path.
• College portal: src is built from the roll number, for example photos/2021045.jpg.
• Image gallery: clicking a small thumbnail changes the src of the big image using JavaScript.
• Wikipedia: every picture points to an upload.wikimedia.org url with the size inside the path.
• GitHub README: badges are <img> tags whose src points to shields.io.
codeExamples: Product gallery, Flipkart style

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• src is resolved against the document base url, or against <base href> when that tag is present.
• When srcset is also given, src becomes the fallback and the browser may pick another candidate. The final choice is readable as currentSrc.
• Setting src in JavaScript starts a fetch immediately, even if the element is not in the DOM.
• Setting src to an empty string is invalid and historically caused a second request for the page url itself.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To drive an image CDN pipeline, where width, quality and format are query parameters on the src.
• To support content hashing, so a build tool writes logo.a91f3c.png and the CDN can cache it forever.
• To implement placeholders, retries and fallbacks in a single place.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Wrong protocol, mixed content or a missing CORS header on a src url silently kills images in production.
• Content Security Policy img-src decides which src hosts are even allowed to load.
• Interview question: what is currentSrc, and why can it differ from the src attribute.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Immutable caching. A hashed src can be cached for one year, which removes repeat downloads.
• Server side resizing. Query parameters on the src let the CDN return the exact needed size.
• Single point of control. A helper function that builds every src can add format, quality and version rules in one place.
• Testable. currentSrc lets automated tests assert that the right variant was chosen.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Cache poisoning risk when a mutable name like logo.png is cached for a long time.
• Infinite loop if the error handler sets a placeholder src that is also missing.
• CSP breakage. Adding a new CDN without updating img-src makes every image disappear.
• Query parameter explosion on the CDN creates many cache keys for the same picture and lowers the hit rate.
• Data urls bypass caching and inflate the HTML, which hurts the first paint.

6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Flipkart and Myntra: src carries the size inside the path, for example /image/416/416/product.jpg, so the CDN caches a small set of fixed sizes.
• Wikipedia: thumbnail urls contain the pixel width, which lets the image server generate and cache exactly that variant.
• Next.js and other frameworks: the image component rewrites src into an optimizer route that returns webp or avif based on the Accept header.
• Banking portals: a strict CSP img-src allows only the bank CDN, so a stolen script cannot leak data through an image url.
• College result portal: when the student photo is missing, the error handler swaps in a neutral avatar and logs the roll number for the admin team.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• alt means alternative text. It is a short text description of the picture.
• The browser shows this text when the image file cannot load.
• A screen reader speaks this text to a blind user, so alt is their only way to know the picture.
• For a decorative picture we write an empty alt, that is alt equal to two quotes with nothing inside.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To make the website usable by people who cannot see.
• To still give useful information when the network fails and images do not load.
• To help Google understand the picture, which improves image search results.

3. Need of This Topic

• Indian government and banking sites must follow accessibility rules, and alt is the first check.
• In India many users are on slow networks where images often fail, alt saves the page.
• It is a very common interview question, and missing alt is the top issue in every audit tool.

4. Advantages

• Accessibility. Blind and low vision users can understand the page.
• Fallback. The meaning survives even when the image does not load.
• SEO. Google reads alt text and shows the picture in image search.
• Free. It costs nothing, just a few words while writing the tag.
• Legal safety. It helps meet accessibility rules that many companies must follow.

5. Disadvantages

• Easy to write badly. Text like photo1 or best product is worse than useless.
• Too long alt is painful to hear, a screen reader has no way to skip in the middle.
• Keyword stuffing for SEO is treated as spam by search engines.
• Maintenance work. When the picture changes, someone must remember to change the alt too.
• Wrong on decorative images. Alt on every small icon makes the page noisy for screen reader users.
codeExamples: Sales grew from Rs 4 lakh in January to Rs 11 lakh in December.

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart: alt on a product photo repeats the product title so the listing makes sense without images.
• Amazon: the small star rating picture carries alt like 4.3 out of 5 stars.
• College portal: the student photo has alt like Photo of Anjali Deshmukh, roll number 2021045.
• Wikipedia: every article photo has a careful description written by editors.
• GitHub: a build badge has alt like Build status passing.
• Bank site: the captcha refresh icon has alt like Get a new captcha image.

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• alt supplies the element accessible name for an image in the accessibility tree.
• alt equal to empty maps the image to role presentation, so assistive technology skips it. Missing alt is different, the screen reader may then read the file name.
• When an image is the only content of a link or a button, alt describes the action, not the picture.
• aria-label, aria-labelledby or a figcaption reference can override alt, and the naming order matters.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To pass WCAG 1.1.1 Non text Content, which is a legal requirement for government and banking portals.
• To let automated CI checks such as axe or Lighthouse gate a release.
• To decide the correct pattern for complex images: short alt plus a long description elsewhere.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Accessibility defects are expensive to fix late, so the rules must be part of code review.
• Charts, maps and infographics need a documented long description strategy, not just alt.
• Interview question: what is the difference between a missing alt, an empty alt and role presentation.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Machine checkable. A missing alt is caught automatically by axe, Lighthouse or an eslint jsx-a11y rule.
• Cheap compliance. It is the single highest value accessibility fix per minute spent.
• Better SEO signal for image search, and a real ranking benefit for e commerce catalogues.
• Works with server rendering. Alt text can be generated from the product title in the template, so it never goes stale.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Automation cannot judge quality. A tool sees alt equal to image as a pass, though it helps nobody.
• Auto generated alt from a catalogue field can produce very long or duplicated names across a grid.
• Conflicting names. aria-label silently overrides alt, which causes confusing audit results.
• Localisation cost. Alt text must be translated for every language the site supports.
• Not enough for charts. Complex data images still need a table or a long description.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The width attribute tells the browser how wide the image should be, in CSS pixels.
• We write only the number, for example width equal to 300. We never write px inside the attribute.
• It is a hint about the real size of the file, so the browser can keep space for the image before it arrives.
• CSS can override it later, but the attribute still helps during loading.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To stop the page from jumping while pictures are still downloading.
• To keep all product cards in a Flipkart style grid the same size.
• To show a large photo as a small thumbnail in a cart or a list.

3. Need of This Topic

• On a slow Indian mobile network a page without width jumps a lot and users tap the wrong button.
• Google measures this jumping as Cumulative Layout Shift and it affects ranking.
• Interviewers ask why width should be given in HTML when CSS is already there.

4. Advantages

• No layout jump. The browser reserves the space before the picture arrives.
• Consistent design. All thumbnails look equal in a grid.
• Works without CSS. Even if the stylesheet fails to load, sizes are still sensible.
• Aspect ratio. Modern browsers use width and height together to compute the ratio automatically.

5. Disadvantages

• Not responsive by itself. A fixed width of 1200 overflows a small mobile screen.
• Stretching. If you give only width and the value does not match the file, the picture can look squeezed when height is also forced.
• No bandwidth saving. Showing a 4000 pixel photo at width 100 still downloads the full heavy file.
• Mixing styles. If CSS sets a different width, students get confused about which one wins.

6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart grid: every card image is set to the same width so the rows stay straight.
• Amazon cart: width 60 thumbnails beside each item.
• College portal: the student photo is fixed at width 120 for the ID card layout.
• Wikipedia: the info box picture is fixed near width 220.
• GitHub: avatars are width 40 in the commit list and width 260 on the profile.

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• The width attribute is a presentational hint with very low specificity, so any CSS rule beats it.
• Since 2020 browsers use width and height to compute a default aspect ratio, so with CSS height auto the space is reserved correctly at every screen size.
• In the DOM, img.width returns the current layout width, while img.naturalWidth returns the true pixel width of the file.
• With srcset the attribute value should match the fallback src variant, since the ratio is what matters.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To drive the aspect ratio box that removes CLS in responsive layouts.
• To let build tools inject exact dimensions from the image file automatically.
• To keep grid virtualization and infinite scroll stable, since row heights become predictable.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• CLS is one of the three Core Web Vitals and a missing width is its most common cause.
• Server side rendered pages must ship dimensions in the HTML, since JavaScript runs too late to help.
• Interview question: how do width and height prevent layout shift when the CSS says width 100 percent.

4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Zero cost CLS fix. Adding two attributes often takes a page from a poor CLS score to a good one.
• Automatable. Build plugins read the file header and inject width and height at compile time.
• Ratio aware. Works together with CSS aspect-ratio and object-fit for art directed crops.
• Improves scroll performance. Known row heights mean fewer relayouts during infinite scroll.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Stale values. If a designer replaces the file with a different ratio and nobody updates the attribute, the image is distorted or the reserved box is wrong.
• Conflicts with srcset when variants have different ratios, since only one ratio can be declared.
• Ignored under some CSS. With width fixed in CSS and height auto missing, the ratio benefit disappears.
• No effect on payload. A small width does not make the download smaller, only srcset and a CDN can do that.
• User agent differences for very old browsers that do not implement the ratio behaviour.

6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Flipkart and Myntra: catalogue tiles declare a fixed ratio, so a hundred product cards render without a single pixel of shift while scrolling.
• Amazon: the main product image reserves its box before the zoom script loads, which keeps the buy button in a stable place.
• News portals: ad slots and article images both declare sizes, since a shifting article is the classic reason users misclick.
• Static site generators: a markdown image plugin reads the file header and writes width and height into the built HTML automatically.
• Wikipedia: thumbnail width is part of the url and the same number is written into the attribute, so the two never disagree.
• College result portal: the marksheet list reserves 120 by 150 for every photo, so printing gives the same layout every time.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The height attribute tells the browser how tall the image should be, in CSS pixels.
• We write only the number, for example height equal to 200. No px and no percent sign.
• It is always used together with width. The pair tells the browser the shape of the picture.
• The browser uses this pair to keep an empty box ready while the file is still downloading.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To reserve vertical space so the text below the picture does not jump down suddenly.
• To keep every banner in a slider exactly the same height.
• To make ID card and marksheet photos print at a fixed size.

3. Need of This Topic

• When only width is given, the browser still does not know the height until the file arrives on slow networks.
• Layout jumping is measured by Google and it lowers your page score.
• Interviewers ask why both width and height must be written even when CSS controls the size.

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• No downward jump. Content below the picture stays in place.
• Even rows. Product cards and slider slides all look the same height.
• Ratio hint. With width it gives the browser the shape of the picture.
• Print friendly. Marksheets and ID cards print at a predictable size.

5. Disadvantages

• Distortion. A wrong height with a fixed width squeezes or stretches faces.
• Not responsive. A fixed height cuts or letterboxes the picture on a mobile screen.
• Fights with CSS. If CSS sets height auto, the attribute value is only a ratio hint, which confuses beginners.
• No download saving. A small height does not reduce the file size at all.

6. Real Time Examples

• Flipkart slider: every home page banner is coded at the same height so the page does not shake while it rotates.
• Amazon: cart thumbnails are 60 by 60, so all rows have equal height.
• College portal: the photo box is 120 by 150, matching the passport photo rule.
• Wikipedia: the info box picture declares its height so the article text does not shift.
• GitHub: avatars are 40 by 40 in the timeline, so the commit list scrolls smoothly.
• News sites: article images declare height so an ad loading above does not push the story down.
