• Use responsive design for better mobile view.
codeExamples:
Employee Details
Name Department Salary
Jiva IT $5000
Jane HR $4500
Mike Finance $6000

expert.content:
Using thead, tbody and tfoot

• < thead > is used to group table header content.
• < tbody > is used to group the main body content.
• < tfoot > is used to group footer content (totals, summary).
• Improves structure and accessibility.
codeExamples:
Product Quantity Price
Laptop 2 50000
Mouse 5 500
Total 102500

expert.content:
Responsive Table (Mobile Friendly)

• Wrap table inside a div.
• Use overflow-x: auto for horizontal scrolling.
• Useful when table has many columns.
codeExamples:
ID Name Email Phone Address
1 Jiva john@email.com 9999999999 New York

expert.content:
Real-World Product Report Table

• Alternate row coloring using nth-child.
• Hover effect for better UX.
• Clean professional UI.
codeExamples:
Monthly Sales Report
Product ID Product Name Category Quantity Sold Total Revenue
101 Laptop Electronics 10 500000
102 Mobile Electronics 25 375000
103 Chair Furniture 15 75000
Grand Total 950000

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The table element displays data in rows and columns.
• It is meant for tabular data such as schedules, prices and results, not for page layout.
• A table is built from rows (tr) that contain cells (th and td).
• Browsers draw no borders by default, so you add them with CSS.

Key Points

• The minimum structure is table, tr and td.
• Rows run left to right and columns are formed by the cells in each row.
• Every row should have the same number of cells unless you use colspan or rowspan.
• Text inside a table follows the normal inline rules of its cell.
codeExamples:
CourseLevel
Core JavaBeginner
Spring BootIntermediate

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use border-collapse: collapse so adjacent borders merge into one line.
• Set the width with CSS, for example width: 100%, and let columns share the space.
• Style rows with tr:nth-child(even) to create zebra stripes.
• Wrap wide tables in a div with overflow-x: auto so phones can scroll sideways.

Common Mistakes

• Using tables for page layout. CSS grid and flexbox are the proper tools.
• Leaving out th cells, which loses the meaning of each column for assistive tools.
• Using the old border, cellpadding and width attributes instead of CSS.
• Rows with different cell counts that break the grid.

Try It Yourself

• Build a table of three courses with columns for name, hours and level. Add zebra stripes with CSS and then wrap it so it scrolls sideways on a narrow screen.
codeExamples:
TopicLessonsHours
HTML12012
CSS14015
Java20030

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Pricing comparisons, timetables and report pages all rely on tables.
• Data from an API is often turned into table rows with JavaScript.
• Email clients still use tables for layout, which is an exception to the rule.
• Accessible data tables help screen reader users move cell by cell.

Best Practices

• Use a table only when the data has more than one dimension.
• Add a caption and header cells to every data table.
• Keep cells short, and move long content to a link or a details element.
• Test with the keyboard and a screen reader on important tables.

Interview Question

• Q: When should you use a table instead of a list?
• A: Use a table when each item has several attributes that readers want to compare across rows and columns. Use a list for one-dimensional sequences.
codeExamples:
Course overview
CourseHours
HTML12

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The caption element gives a table a visible title.
• It must be the first child of the table element.
• Screen readers announce it when the user reaches the table.
• It is the proper way to label a table, instead of a paragraph above it.

Key Points

• Write a short, clear description such as "Monthly sales, 2026".
• By default the caption appears above the table, centred.
• Move it below with the CSS caption-side: bottom.
• Only one caption is allowed per table.
codeExamples:
Course schedule
DayTopic
MondayHTML
TuesdayCSS

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Style the caption like any block: font size, colour, alignment and padding.
• text-align controls its horizontal position within the table width.
• When the table sits in a figure, you may use figcaption instead for a caption that covers more than the table.
• Combine it with aria-describedby to point to a longer description.

Common Mistakes

• Placing a heading above the table instead of a caption, which hides the link between them.
• Putting the caption after the rows, where it is invalid.
• Writing a caption that repeats the page heading word for word.
• Hiding the caption with display none, which also hides it from screen readers.

Try It Yourself

• Add a caption to a table and move it to the bottom with CSS. Then write a second table with a hidden caption and check that a screen reader still announces it.
codeExamples:
Source: JavaSchoolLab, 2026
MonthLearners
Sep1200
Oct1800

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Data tables in reports use a caption for the title and a note below for the source.
• A visually hidden caption is possible through a CSS utility that keeps it available to screen readers.
• Search engines can use captions to understand what the table shows.
• Long tables with captions are easier to find in a screen reader list of tables.

Best Practices

• Keep captions under one short sentence.
• Use the same wording style across your site.
• Leave extra explanation to a paragraph referenced with aria-describedby.
• Make sure the caption makes sense out of context.

Interview Question

• Q: Why use caption instead of a heading above the table?
• A: The caption is programmatically linked to its table, so assistive technology announces it as the accessible name of the table. A heading is just nearby text.
codeExamples:
Learners are counted at the end of each month.

Monthly learners
MonthLearners
Sep1200

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The thead element groups the header rows of a table.
• It sits at the top, before tbody, and contains one or more tr elements of th cells.
• It tells browsers and tools which rows are headings and not data.
• It is optional but strongly recommended.

Key Points

• When a long table prints across pages, browsers repeat the thead on every page.
• It can be styled as a group, for example with a coloured background.
• It helps assistive technology identify the column headers.
• With JavaScript you can sort only the tbody rows and leave the thead alone.
codeExamples:
NameScore
Asha92
Ravi85

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Make the header stick while scrolling with position: sticky; top: 0 on the th cells.
• Use several rows in thead for grouped headings, combined with colspan.
• Keep the thead in the source above tbody, even though tfoot can come later.
• Do not place td cells in the thead unless they truly are headings.

Common Mistakes

• Putting header rows in tbody, so print and accessibility features do not treat them as headers.
• Adding more than one thead to a table. Only one is allowed.
• Forgetting that sticky headers need a scrolling container with a set height.
• Styling the thead but not the th cells inside it, which may be overridden.

Try It Yourself

• Make a table with a thead of dark cells and six body rows inside a 140px tall scrolling box. Make the header cells sticky and scroll to check that they stay visible.
codeExamples:
#Lesson
1Intro
2Tags
3Lists
4Tables
5Forms
6Media

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Data grids and dashboards use sticky heads so labels stay visible in long lists.
• Reports printed from the browser rely on repeated headers across pages.
• Sortable tables attach click handlers to the th cells in the thead.
• Grouped column headings use two header rows in one thead.

Best Practices

• Always include a thead in data tables.
• Use scope attributes on header cells as well.
• Limit the header to one or two rows for readability.
• Give the header cells a clear contrast against the body rows.

Interview Question

• Q: What does thead do for printing?
• A: When a table spans several printed pages, browsers repeat the thead at the top of each page, so readers always see the column names.
codeExamples:
NameMarks
TheoryPractical
Asha4548

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The tbody element groups the main data rows of a table.
• It comes after thead and before tfoot.
• If you leave it out, the browser creates one for you automatically.
• A table can contain several tbody elements to separate groups of rows.

Key Points

• It makes the structure explicit: head, body and foot.
• You can style the whole group, for example with a background colour.
• JavaScript targets it when adding or removing rows, using tbody.append(row).
• It does not change the display of the table by itself.
codeExamples:
ItemPrice
Notebook50
Pen10

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use several tbody elements to group related rows, such as one per category.
• Add a border above each group with tbody + tbody.
• Because browsers insert tbody automatically, the selector table > tr never matches. Use table tr or tbody tr.
• Create new rows with insertRow() on the tbody.

Common Mistakes

• Expecting table > tr in CSS to select rows. The auto-created tbody sits in between.
• Putting a tr directly inside table in the DOM with createElement and wondering about the layout.
• Using more than one tbody just for styling with no meaning.
• Appending rows to the table instead of the tbody in scripts.

Try It Yourself

• Create a table with two tbody groups, each starting with a heading row. Add a thicker border between groups and a button that appends a new row to the first group.
codeExamples:
Fruits
Apple120
Vegetables
Carrot40

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Dynamic tables add rows to the tbody as data arrives from an API.
• Grouped bodies are used for financial statements and category lists.
• Row virtualisation libraries manage only the tbody contents.
• Sorting and filtering scripts reorder the rows inside tbody.

Best Practices

• Always write tbody explicitly so your markup matches the DOM.
• Use one tbody for simple tables and several for grouped data.
• Keep scripts targeting tbody and not table.
• Avoid heavy markup inside cells for large tables.

Interview Question

• Q: Why does the selector table > tr not match rows in the browser?
• A: The HTML parser inserts a tbody between table and tr automatically, so tr is a child of tbody, not of table.
codeExamples: Existing row

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The tfoot element groups the summary rows at the bottom of a table.
• It is typically used for totals, averages or notes.
• It may be written before or after tbody in the source, but it always displays at the bottom.
• There can be only one tfoot per table.

Key Points

• It holds tr rows with td or th cells like the other sections.
• It helps browsers repeat the footer on printed pages.
• You can style it with a top border and a bold font.
• Assistive technology can tell that these cells summarise the data above.
codeExamples:
ItemPrice
Notebook50
Pen10
Total60

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Right-align number columns, including the totals, so digits line up.
• Use colspan to let the label cell span the leading columns.
• Compute totals with JavaScript and write them into the tfoot cells.
• Use a double top border to show a total line like an invoice.

Common Mistakes

• Placing tfoot inside tbody, which is invalid.
• Using more than one tfoot in a single table.
• Making the totals manually and forgetting to update them.
• Using the footer for notes that are not part of the data.

Try It Yourself

• Build a small invoice with three items and a tfoot total. Right-align the numbers and add a double border above the total row.
codeExamples:
ItemQtyAmount
Course pass21998
Workbook1250
Total2248

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Invoices, shopping carts and financial reports use tfoot for totals.
• Dashboards place column averages or counts there.
• Printed reports repeat it on each page when needed.
• Totals can be computed on the server or with a short script.

Best Practices

• Format numbers consistently with the same decimals.
• Align totals with the numbers they sum.
• Add an accessible label such as Total in the first cell.
• Keep the footer to one or two rows.

Interview Question

• Q: Where does tfoot appear if you write it before tbody?
• A: It still renders at the bottom of the table. HTML5 allows either position in the source, and browsers always place it last.
codeExamples:
A10
B25
Total

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The tr element defines one row of a table.
• Its children are th and td cells, laid out from left to right.
• Rows can sit inside thead, tbody, tfoot or directly in the table.
• The row is the main unit you style, add and remove.

Key Points

• All rows should end up with the same number of columns.
• Cells created by colspan count for several columns.
• Rows have no width of their own; the cells decide it.
• tr supports background, border and height styling.
codeExamples:
NameCity
AshaPune
RaviMumbai

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use tr:hover to highlight the row under the pointer.
• Use tr:nth-child(odd) for stripes and tr:last-child for the final row.
• Row height can be set with the CSS height property, which acts as a minimum.
• Use data attributes such as data-id on the row to connect it to a record.

Common Mistakes

• Trying to set the width on tr. Set it on the cells or columns instead.
• Placing text directly inside a tr without a cell.
• Using margin on rows. It has no effect in a table.
• Forgetting to close rows, which can swallow the next row.

Try It Yourself

• Create a table with five rows. Highlight the row under the mouse, stripe even rows and toggle a selected state when a row is clicked.
codeExamples:
NameCity
AshaPune
RaviMumbai
MeenaDelhi

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Clickable rows open a detail page and need keyboard access through a link in one cell.
• Selected rows are marked with a class or aria-selected attribute.
• Row actions such as edit and delete live in the last cell.
• Rows are the unit that scripts sort, filter and paginate.

Best Practices

• Make the whole row clickable with a link inside, not with an onclick on tr alone.
• Use aria-selected for selectable grids.
• Keep row heights consistent for readability.
• Avoid very long rows. Move extra data to a detail view.

Interview Question

• Q: What can you not style on a tr element?
• A: Margin and padding have no effect on rows. Spacing is controlled with the cells, or with border-spacing on the table when borders are separate.
codeExamples:
Java
HTML
CSS

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The th element defines a header cell for a column or row.
• Browsers show its text bold and centred by default.
• Screen readers use it to announce the heading before each data cell.
• It can appear in thead, tbody and tfoot.

Key Points

• Use scope="col" for a column header and scope="row" for a row header.
• A th is a real cell, so colspan and rowspan work on it.
• Do not use td with bold styling in place of th.
• Row headers help in tables where the first column names each row.
codeExamples:
NameAge
Asha21

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use th scope="row" in the first cell of each row for a two-way table.
• Use the abbr attribute to give a short version of long headings for screen readers.
• The headers attribute links a data cell to specific header ids in complex tables.
• Align header text with its data: numbers to the right, text to the left.

Common Mistakes

• Making headers with td and CSS, so assistive tools see no headers.
• Leaving the first cell of a table empty without a hidden label.
• Forgetting scope in tables with headers on both axes.
• Assuming bold centred text is the only effect. The semantic role matters most.

Try It Yourself

• Make a weekly timetable with column headers for days and row headers for subjects. Use scope on every header and give the empty corner cell a hidden label.
codeExamples:
MonTue
HTML2h1h
CSS1h3h

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Timetables and comparison charts need both row and column headers.
• Screen readers read "HTML, Monday, 2h" when the headers are marked up well.
• Sortable tables put buttons inside th cells.
• Sticky first columns use th scope="row" cells.

Best Practices

• Every data table needs header cells.
• Add a visually hidden label for an empty corner cell.
• Keep headings short and unique.
• Use aria-sort on sortable headers.

Interview Question

• Q: What does the scope attribute on th do?
• A: It states whether the header applies to a column, a row or groups of them, so screen readers announce the right header for each data cell.
codeExamples:
Score
Asha92

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The td element defines a data cell inside a row.
• It holds the actual values: text, numbers, links, images or other content.
• The browser aligns it left by default, with a small padding.
• Cells in one column share the same width automatically.

Key Points

• A td can contain any flow content, such as lists and buttons.
• Use colspan and rowspan to let a cell cover several columns or rows.
• The vertical alignment is middle by default and can be changed with CSS.
• The closing tag is optional but you should always write it.
codeExamples:
ItemPrice
Notebook50
Pen set10

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use text-align: right on numeric cells so digits align.
• Use vertical-align: top when cells hold multiple lines of text.
• Use white-space: nowrap to keep short values like dates on one line.
• Use text-overflow: ellipsis with a max-width for very long text.

Common Mistakes

• Putting block layouts inside cells, creating tables within tables.
• Setting widths on every cell instead of the column or table.
• Leaving cells empty without meaning. Use a dash or a visually hidden note.
• Mixing units in one column, which confuses readers.

Try It Yourself

• Create a table with a numeric column that is right aligned with tabular figures, and a long text cell that is cut with an ellipsis and shows the full text as a tooltip.
codeExamples:
ItemAmount
Fees1,250.00
Books98.50

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Cells often hold buttons, badges and avatars in dashboards.
• Data bound tables write td content from JSON with textContent to stay safe.
• Truncated text in cells shows its full value in a title attribute.
• Tabular numbers keep columns of figures aligned.

Best Practices

• Always escape or set text safely when filling cells from user data.
• Use consistent alignment per column.
• Keep the content of each cell short.
• Add a header cell for each column that holds data.

Interview Question

• Q: What is the difference between th and td?
• A: th is a header cell that describes a column or row, and td is a data cell. The distinction gives assistive technology the structure of the table.
codeExamples:
Title
Introduction to semantic HTML elements and accessibility

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The rowspan attribute makes a cell stretch down across several rows.
• The value is the number of rows the cell covers.
• It applies to td and th elements.
• The rows below must leave out the cells that are now covered.

Key Points

• rowspan="2" covers the current row and the next one.
• The covered cell positions are skipped in the rows below.
• Use it for merged labels, such as a category that spans its items.
• A value of 0 once meant the rest of the section, but is no longer supported widely.
codeExamples:
GroupItem
FruitsApple
Banana
VegetableCarrot

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Count the columns carefully in each row after a span so the grid stays aligned.
• Combine rowspan and colspan for complex headers.
• Use vertical-align to centre the spanning cell content.
• Test the table in different browsers, since overlapping spans are handled differently.

Common Mistakes

• Adding the covered cell anyway, which pushes the row one column too wide.
• Spanning past the end of the row group, such as beyond thead.
• Using rowspan to create visual layouts rather than data relationships.
• Overusing spans, which makes the table hard for screen readers to follow.

Try It Yourself

• Make a table of regions and cities where the region cell spans two rows. Then build a small timetable where one lesson lasts two periods using rowspan.
codeExamples:
RegionCitySales
WestPune120
Mumbai200
NorthDelhi180
Jaipur90

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Timetables use rowspan for lessons that last two periods.
• Reports group rows by category in the first column.
• Spanning cells must be tested for accessibility with a screen reader.
• Spans should not cross thead, tbody and tfoot boundaries.

Best Practices

• Keep spans simple and small.
• Prefer separate nested tables or grouped tbody elements for complex data.
• Use th with scope rowgroup where it fits.
• Review the table in a browser outline view to make sure every row has the right cells.

Interview Question

• Q: If a cell has rowspan=2, what must you do in the next row?
• A: Omit one cell from it, because the spanning cell already occupies that column position in the next row.
codeExamples:
TimeMonTue
9:00Java Lab (2h)HTML
10:00CSS

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The colspan attribute makes a cell stretch across several columns.
• The value is the number of columns the cell covers.
• It works on td and th.
• The row then needs fewer cells to complete the grid.

Key Points

• colspan="2" merges the current column with the next one.
• A row with a colspan cell has fewer cell elements than the others.
• It is typical for group headings and total labels.
• Use it with rowspan to build multi-level headers.
codeExamples:
Contact
Emailteam@example.com
Phone+91 20 1234 5678

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use colspan on header cells to group columns, such as "Marks" over "Theory" and "Practical".
• Add scope="colgroup" to the spanning header to tell assistive tools what it covers.
• Centre spanning headings with text-align to show they cover several columns.
• Make sure the total of spans plus other cells matches in every row.

Common Mistakes

• Using too many cells in a row after a span, which adds extra columns.
• Spanning over columns that hold unrelated data.
• Using colspan to centre content, where CSS alignment is better.
• Forgetting to update spans when you add a column.

Try It Yourself

• Create a marks table with a Marks heading that spans Theory and Practical columns. Add a footer row whose label cell spans two columns.
codeExamples:
NameMarks
TheoryPractical
Asha4548
Ravi4042

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Grouped column headings are standard in financial and exam reports.
• Footers use colspan for a long label next to a total.
• Calendars use spans for events across several days.
• Data export tools generate colspan for merged headings.

Best Practices

• Keep the grid regular where possible, since merged cells make sorting hard.
• Test with a screen reader to confirm headers are announced.
• Use colgroup and col for styling whole columns instead of repeating classes.
• Document the column structure for future editors.

Interview Question

• Q: How do you build a two-level column heading?
• A: Use a colspan header cell on the first row for the group and a second row of normal headers beneath it, adding rowspan to the cells that have no sub-headings.
codeExamples:
ItemQtyPrice
Book2500
Total500

beginner.content:
What It Is

• Table headers label the columns and rows so that each data cell has meaning.
• They are marked with th elements, not with styled td cells.
• Good headers let readers and assistive tools understand a table at a glance.
• Simple tables need only column headers; others need row headers as well.

Key Points

• Use scope="col" and scope="row" on header cells.
• The headers attribute connects a data cell to header ids in irregular tables.
• The id of each th is referenced from the td headers list.
• Keep header text short and unique.
codeExamples:
CourseHours
HTML12

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use the id and headers pair when a table has multi-level headings that scope cannot express.
• Screen readers read the full path, such as "Marks, Theory, 45".
• Test with NVDA or VoiceOver to verify that the right headers are spoken.
• Hide an empty corner cell label with a visually hidden span.

Common Mistakes

• Using only visual styling to show headers.
• Giving two headers the same text, which makes reading ambiguous.
• Using headers ids that do not exist.
• Using headers on simple tables where scope is enough.

Try It Yourself

• Build a marks table with a two-level header and add scope to a simple version. Then use id and headers to link each data cell in the complex one.
codeExamples:
NameMarks
TheoryPractical
Asha4548

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Government and finance sites publish complex tables with headers ids for accessibility.
• Automated checkers flag tables that lack header cells.
• Mobile layouts that turn rows into cards must keep the header relationship, for example with data-label.
• Good headers also help search engines pick tables for snippets.

Best Practices

• Prefer simple tables that need only scope.
• Split very complex tables into several smaller tables.
• Run an accessibility checker on every data table.
• Keep the header row visible when scrolling.

Interview Question

• Q: When do you need the headers attribute instead of scope?
• A: When a table has irregular or multi-level headings that scope cannot describe, so each data cell lists the ids of its headers explicitly.
codeExamples:
CourseHours
HTML12

beginner.content:
What It Is

• An accessible table can be understood and used by people with screen readers and keyboards.
• It relies on proper structure: caption, thead, th and scope.
• Good structure also helps everyone else, including search engines.
• Accessibility is built with markup, not with styling.

Key Points

• Add a caption that names the table.
• Use th with scope for every header.
• Group rows with thead, tbody and tfoot.
• Avoid merged cells unless they are really needed.
codeExamples:
Course hours per week
CourseHours
HTML3

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use aria-describedby to connect a longer explanation to the table.
• Make wide tables keyboard scrollable by adding tabindex="0" and a label to the scroll container.
• Ensure enough colour contrast between text and row stripes.
• Do not remove header semantics when restyling tables as cards on small screens.

Common Mistakes

• Using display: block on table parts without restoring roles, which removes table semantics in some browsers.
• Relying on colour alone to show status, such as red and green.
• Leaving empty header cells with no label.
• Creating layout tables that screen readers announce as data tables.

Try It Yourself

• Take a table of your own and add a caption, scope on every header, and a status column that shows text as well as colour. Test it with the keyboard only.
codeExamples:
Fees by course
CourseQ1Q2Q3Q4
Java1000100012001200

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Public service sites must meet WCAG rules, so their tables are tested carefully.
• Responsive designs keep table roles when stacking cells on phones.
• Status columns combine colour with text such as Passed or Failed.
• Large datasets use ARIA grid patterns only when they need editing behaviour.

Best Practices

• Test with a screen reader and the keyboard.
• Keep tables simple and single purpose.
• Prefer text status over colour-only status.
• Document the table structure in your design system.

Interview Question

• Q: What makes a table accessible at minimum?
• A: A caption, header cells with scope, sensible grouping with thead and tbody, and no layout use. Together these let screen readers announce each cell with its headers.
codeExamples:
Test results
SuiteStatus
Unit✓ Passed
UI✗ Failed

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The scope attribute on a th cell says which cells the header applies to.
• The values are col, row, colgroup and rowgroup.
• Screen readers use it to read the right header with each data cell.
• It is simple, fast to add and the first tool for accessible tables.

Key Points

• scope="col" marks a column header.
• scope="row" marks a row header.
• colgroup and rowgroup apply to grouped headings that span several columns or rows.
• It is only valid on th elements.
codeExamples:
Q1Q2
Sales1014
Costs68

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use scope on every th in a table that has headers on both axes.
• Use colgroup for a heading that spans two columns through colspan.
• Use rowgroup for a row heading that spans several rows through rowspan.
• Modern browsers can often guess scope, but explicit markup is more reliable.

Common Mistakes

• Putting scope on td cells, where it is obsolete.
• Using scope on very irregular tables where headers ids are better.
• Using the wrong value, such as col for a row header.
• Forgetting scope in the first column that acts as a header.

Try It Yourself

• Write a table with headers on both axes and mark each header with the correct scope. Then add a grouped heading that spans two columns and use colgroup.
codeExamples:
2026
H1H2
Revenue4055

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Government and education sites apply scope everywhere because auditors check for it.
• Content management systems add it automatically when editors mark a header row.
• Automated tests flag th cells that lack scope in complex tables.
• Design systems include scope in their table components.

Best Practices

• Make scope a part of your table component.
• Test with a screen reader that supports table navigation.
• Keep header text short so it is pleasant to hear repeatedly.
• Use headers ids only when scope cannot describe the structure.

Interview Question

• Q: What are the possible values of scope?
• A: col, row, colgroup and rowgroup. The first two cover simple headers, and the group values cover headers spanning several columns or rows.
codeExamples:
WestPune120
Mumbai200

beginner.content:
What It Is

• Column groups let you apply styles or attributes to whole columns of a table.
• They are made with colgroup and col elements placed at the start of the table.
• Without them, you would style every cell of a column by hand.
• They describe columns, while rows are described by tr.

Key Points

• colgroup goes right after caption and before thead or tr.
• Each col inside stands for one column, or several with the span attribute.
• Only a few properties work on columns: background, border, width and visibility.
• Cells in a column inherit those styles.
codeExamples:
NameMathScience
Asha9088

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Set a column width with col { width: 120px } in table-layout fixed tables.
• Highlight the sorted column by changing the class on its col element.
• Use visibility: collapse to hide a column in some browsers.
• Use several colgroups to separate logical sections of columns.

Common Mistakes

• Expecting padding or colour of text to work on col. Only a few properties apply.
• Placing colgroup after the rows.
• Mixing the span attribute and individual col elements wrongly.
• Leaving a column out, so styles land on the wrong one.

Try It Yourself

• Make a three column table with fixed widths set through col elements and a shaded middle column. Then toggle a highlight class on a col with a button.
codeExamples:
TitleHoursLevel
Introduction to Java10Basic

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Data grids set column widths through colgroup for faster rendering with table-layout fixed.
• Financial tables shade the total column.
• Print stylesheets hide optional columns.
• Scripts toggle a class on col to highlight a column on hover.

Best Practices

• Use col for width and background only.
• Keep the number of col elements in step with the columns.
• Prefer CSS classes on cells when you need text styles.
• Document which columns are fixed width.

Interview Question

• Q: Why would you use colgroup instead of styling each td?
• A: One col rule styles an entire column in a single place, which is shorter, faster and easier to change than adding a class to every cell.
codeExamples:
AB (highlighted)C
123

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The colgroup element groups one or more col elements that describe columns.
• It must be a child of table, placed before the table rows.
• It can also use the span attribute when it has no col children.
• It affects only the columns, not the cell content.

Key Points

• The span attribute sets how many columns the group covers.
• Use several colgroup elements to label different parts of the table.
• A group is a convenient hook for a background across the columns.
• It must come after caption if one exists.
codeExamples:
NameCityScore
AshaPune92

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use a colgroup for each logical block, such as identity columns and result columns.
• Give each group a class to style it from your stylesheet.
• Combine with a thicker border on the first cell of each group.
• Remember that a group with span cannot also hold col children.

Common Mistakes

• Putting colgroup inside thead or tbody.
• Setting span and also adding col elements in the same group.
• Writing colgroup after tr rows, which is invalid.
• Expecting border styles on colgroup to render in every browser.

Try It Yourself

• Create a table with two colgroups: one for the first two columns and one for the last two. Shade each group in a different colour.
codeExamples:
NameCityMathScience
AshaPune9088

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Statements with many columns use groups to show related columns together.
• Spreadsheet-like pages keep the first group fixed while scrolling.
• Printing styles collapse unneeded groups.
• Scripts highlight a whole group when the pointer enters it.

Best Practices

• Group columns only when it adds clarity.
• Add a matching colspan header cell above each group.
• Keep the HTML valid by following the order of table children.
• Check results in more than one browser.

Interview Question

• Q: What is the correct position of colgroup in a table?
• A: Directly inside table, after an optional caption and before thead, tbody, tfoot or tr elements.
codeExamples:
TitleHoursLevel
Java Basics12Basic

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The col element represents one column inside a colgroup.
• It is a void element and has no closing tag.
• It can carry a class, width or background that applies to every cell in that column.
• The span attribute lets one col stand for several columns.

Key Points

• It must be inside a colgroup, not directly in the table.
• It has no content, only styling and span.
• A few CSS properties apply: width, background, border and visibility.
• Cells with colspan are affected by every column they cover.
codeExamples:
CourseHours
Core Java30

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Set alignment on the cells, for example with td:nth-child(2), because text-align on a col has no effect.
• Use width on col together with table-layout fixed for predictable layouts.
• Add a class with a background to mark an active or sorted column.
• Use span to apply the same width to several equal columns.

Common Mistakes

• Expecting font or text alignment rules on col to work. Browsers ignore them.
• Giving col a closing tag or children.
• Leaving out col elements for some columns, so rules apply to the wrong ones.
• Using margins or padding on col.

• Responsive tables hide a col on small screens together with matching cells.

Best Practices

• Keep col rules small and purposeful.
• Align text through cell rules such as td:nth-child.
• Check that the count of col elements matches the columns.
• Prefer CSS classes for anything col cannot style.

Interview Question

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The <form> element is a container that collects user input and sends it to a server.
• Everything the user fills in, such as <input>, <select> and <textarea>, must sit inside a form if you want the browser to submit it.
• A form has a name and value pair for every control. The name attribute becomes the key, and what the user types becomes the value.
• Without a name attribute a control is simply ignored at submission time.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To learn the standard way a web page talks back to a server without writing any JavaScript.
• To understand that the form element decides where data goes (action) and how it travels (method).
• To group related fields so that one click on the submit button sends the whole set together.

3. Need of This Topic

• Every login page, college admission page, online shopping checkout and bank request page is a form.
• Browsers give free features to forms such as validation, the Enter key submitting, autofill and password managers. You get all of this only if you use a real <form> element.
• Screen readers announce a form as a landmark, so keyboard and blind users can jump straight to it.
codeExamples:
College Admission Enquiry

WRONG

RIGHT

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• No JavaScript needed. The browser packs the data and sends it for you.
• Free validation. Attributes such as required and pattern block a bad submit before the network is touched.
• Keyboard friendly. Pressing Enter inside a text box submits the form automatically.
• Autofill and password managers work only with proper forms, which saves users a lot of typing.
• Accessibility. Assistive tools treat a form as one meaningful unit.

5. Disadvantages

• A plain form submit reloads the whole page, which feels slow compared to a background request.
• You cannot nest one form inside another form. The browser silently drops the inner one.
• Client side rules are only a convenience. A user can bypass them with developer tools, so the server must check again.
• Styling the built in error bubbles is very limited across browsers.
codeExamples:
Point 4 Advantage: browser validation with zero JavaScript

Point 5 Disadvantage handled: use two separate forms

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• College admission form: student name, date of birth, Aadhaar number, marks and course choice all sit in one <form> and go to the college server in a single submit.
• Bank net banking login: customer id and password inside a form posted over HTTPS.
• IRCTC ticket search: from station, to station and journey date in a form.
• Amazon or Flipkart address page: house number, city, state and 6 digit PIN code.
• Google search box: a very small form with one search field.
• Restaurant table booking: name, 10 digit mobile number, number of guests and time.
codeExamples: Point 6 Real Time Example: college admission form

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• A <form> is a serialisation boundary. On submit the browser builds an entry list from the form owner's listed controls and encodes it using the enctype.
• A control does not have to be a physical child. The form attribute on a control points to a form id, so a button placed anywhere on the page can still belong to that form.
• Successful control rules decide what is sent. Disabled controls, unchecked boxes and unnamed controls never appear in the payload.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To build forms that survive real production traffic: CSRF protection, idempotency, progressive enhancement and accessibility.
• To treat the HTML form as the fallback and JavaScript as the enhancement, so the feature still works when a script fails to load.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Interviewers ask why client validation is never enough. The answer is that any client can be scripted with curl or Postman.
• Regulated Indian applications such as KYC or exam registration must log server side validation results for audit.
• A form that posts without a CSRF token is an open door for a hostile site to act as the logged in user.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 1: control linked by the form attribute

Format ABCDE1234F

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Progressive enhancement. A working <form> keeps the feature alive even if the JavaScript bundle fails, which is common on weak mobile networks.
• FormData integration. new FormData(formElement) gives you the exact entry list the browser would have sent, so the ajax path and the plain path stay identical.
• Constraint Validation API. checkValidity, reportValidity and setCustomValidity let you reuse native state with your own error UI.
• Autofill quality improves conversion measurably when autocomplete tokens are correct.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Double submit is easy. A slow network invites a second click, so you need an idempotency key or a disabled button after first submit.
• Native validation messages are not announced reliably by every screen reader, so serious apps render their own messages in an aria-live region.
• novalidate turns off all native checks at once, which is convenient but dangerous if the custom code is incomplete.
• Multipart uploads have no built in progress in a plain submit.
codeExamples: Advanced Point 4 and 5

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• UPI payment confirmation: a POST form carrying a CSRF token and an idempotency key so a retry never charges twice.
• Insurance proposal form: forty plus fields split across fieldsets, saved as a draft on every blur event, with the plain form submit kept as the fallback.
• Government exam registration: server re-validates Aadhaar length, category and photo size even though the browser already checked, because the client is never trusted.
• Global checkout at Shopify or Stripe: autocomplete tokens like given-name, family-name, postal-code and cc-number drive the browser and password manager autofill.
• Airline check in: a single form element with a submit button placed in a sticky footer outside the form, linked using the form attribute.

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The action attribute of <form> holds the URL where the form data is sent when the user submits.
• Example: action="/login" sends the data to the login handler on the same website.
• If you leave action out, the browser submits to the current page URL.
• The URL can be relative such as /register, or absolute such as https://api.example.com/register.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To point the form at the correct server program that will read and store the data.
• To separate pages from endpoints. The page the user sees and the URL that processes data are usually different.

3. Need of This Topic

• A form without a correct action is like a letter without an address. The data goes nowhere useful.
• In real projects the same form may post to different actions, for example a draft save URL and a final submit URL.
• Understanding relative and absolute URLs here prevents the very common bug of posting to the wrong folder.
codeExamples:
Point 1: where does the data go?

WRONG

RIGHT

Absolute URL

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Clear routing. One line tells you exactly which server endpoint handles this form.
• Flexible. Relative URLs keep the form working when the site moves to another domain.
• Overridable. A submit button can carry formaction to send the same form to a different URL, for example Save draft versus Publish.
• Works without JavaScript, so the page is testable by simply opening it.

5. Disadvantages

• A wrong relative path is silent. You only find out when the server returns a 404.
• Posting to another domain triggers cross origin rules and normally breaks session cookies.
• If the action URL is built from user input you create an open redirect risk.
• An http action on an https page sends data in plain text, and modern browsers block this mixed content.
codeExamples:
Point 4 Advantage: two destinations, one form

Point 5 Disadvantage

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• IRCTC search: action="/train-search" with method get, so the result page can be bookmarked.
• Bank fund transfer: action="/accounts/transfer" with method post over https.
• College fee payment: the form action points to a payment gateway URL such as the Razorpay or PayU collect endpoint.
• Newsletter box on a blog: action points to a third party service like Mailchimp.
• Admin panel: the same article form uses formaction for Save draft, Preview and Publish.
codeExamples:
Point 6: fee payment routed to a gateway

Point 6: bookmarkable train search

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• The action is resolved against the document base URL, so a <base> tag or a trailing slash difference changes the final target.
• An empty action="" is legal and means the current URL including its query string, which is a classic source of duplicated query parameters.
• formaction on a submit button, and formmethod, formenctype, formtarget and formnovalidate, override the form level attributes for that one button.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To route one form to several server operations without duplicating markup.
• To keep endpoints stable and versioned, for example /api/v2/orders, so old bookmarks and mobile clients keep working.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Open redirect and CSRF. Never build an action URL from a query parameter supplied by the user.
• Cross origin posts do not carry SameSite cookies by default, so a payment gateway integration must use a signed token instead of the session.
• A Content Security Policy form-action directive can restrict where any form on the page is allowed to post, which blocks injected forms.
codeExamples: Advanced Point 1: base URL changes resolution

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• One markup, many operations. formaction removes the need for three near identical forms.
• Testable contract. The action URL is the API contract, so backend and frontend teams can agree on it early.
• Security lever. The CSP form-action directive gives a strong allow list for submission targets.
• Graceful degradation. If your fetch based submit fails you can fall back to form.submit() which uses the same action.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Hard coded absolute URLs break between development, staging and production, so they should come from configuration.
• Cross origin actions lose the session cookie and often the CSRF token, forcing a separate signed payload.
• formaction is easy to miss in a code review. A button silently posting to a delete endpoint is a real incident pattern.
• If the action returns a redirect, the browser turns the POST into a GET, so state kept only in memory is lost. Use the post redirect get pattern deliberately.
codeExamples: Advanced Point 4: fetch enhancement over the same action

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Payment gateway handoff: the action points to the gateway host, the payload carries a server signed hash, and the session cookie is deliberately not relied upon.
• Content management system: one editor form with formaction values for /save-draft, /preview and /publish, each with its own server side permission check.
• Banking: CSP form-action locked to the bank origin so a cross site scripting payload cannot post credentials elsewhere.
• Versioned APIs: the mobile web app posts to /api/v3/kyc while an older embedded webview still posts to /api/v2/kyc.
• Post redirect get: after /orders returns 303 to /orders/1234/thank-you the user can refresh without paying twice.

Advanced Point 6: signed handoff to a payment gateway

Advanced Point 6: post redirect get

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The method attribute says how the browser sends the form data. The two values used in HTML are get and post.
• With get the data is added to the URL after a question mark, for example /search?q=java&page=2.
• With post the data travels in the request body, which the user does not see in the address bar.
• If you do not write method, the browser uses get.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To choose the right way of sending data: get for reading and searching, post for creating and changing.
• To understand why passwords must never travel through a get form.

3. Need of This Topic

• URLs are logged by servers, saved in browser history and shared in chat. Anything in a get URL is effectively public.
• A get URL also has a practical length limit, so a long form must use post.
• Search engines follow get links but never post, so this choice affects what is indexed.
codeExamples:
Point 1: GET puts data in the URL

Point 2 and 3: WRONG, password in a GET form

RIGHT: POST keeps it in the request body

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• GET is bookmarkable and shareable. A train search result or a product filter can be copied and sent to a friend.
• GET is cacheable by browsers and proxies, so repeated searches feel fast.
• POST hides data from the address bar and has no practical size limit, so it suits long forms and file uploads.
• POST is not repeated blindly. The browser warns before resending it on refresh.

5. Disadvantages

• GET data is visible, logged and length limited, so it is wrong for anything private or large.
• POST results cannot be bookmarked, and pressing refresh can cause a duplicate submission.
• Neither method encrypts anything by itself. Only https protects the data on the wire.
• Using GET for an action that changes data is dangerous, because a crawler or a prefetch can trigger it.
codeExamples:
Point 4 Advantage: shareable filter with GET

Point 5 Disadvantage: GET must never change data

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• Google search: method get, so the result URL can be shared.
• Flipkart filters: get, because the filtered listing must be linkable.
• Net banking login and fund transfer: post, always over https.
• College admission submission: post, because it creates a record and carries dozens of fields.
• Resume upload on Naukri: post with a file, which get simply cannot carry.
• IRCTC train list: get for the search, post for the actual booking.
codeExamples:
Point 6: search uses GET

Point 6: booking uses POST

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• HTML forms support only get and post. Verbs such as put, patch and delete need fetch or XMLHttpRequest, or a hidden _method field that the framework translates on the server.
• The method decides the HTTP semantics. GET must be safe and idempotent, meaning it never changes state and can be repeated freely.
• With get the browser discards any existing query string in the action URL and replaces it with the serialised form data.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To align HTTP semantics with caching, retry logic and crawler behaviour rather than picking a method by habit.
• To design safe endpoints where a prefetch, an antivirus link scanner or a corporate proxy cannot cause damage.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Real incidents happen when a delete link is exposed to GET and a browser extension prefetches every link on a page.
• SameSite cookie behaviour differs by method. A cross site POST is blocked with SameSite Lax while a top level GET is allowed.
• Compliance rules for Indian financial apps forbid personal data such as PAN or Aadhaar appearing in URLs, because URLs are stored in access logs.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 1: emulating DELETE with a hidden field

Advanced Point 1: GET wipes the existing query string

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Cache and CDN wins. A GET search endpoint can be cached at the edge, cutting server load dramatically.
• Safe retries. Because GET is idempotent, a proxy or a mobile network can retry it without risk.
• Deep linking and analytics. Query parameters from a GET form feed campaign tracking naturally.
• POST plus post redirect get removes the duplicate submission dialog and gives a clean shareable result URL.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• URL length limits are real. Many proxies stop near 2000 characters, so a big filter set must move to POST or to a saved search id.
• POST responses are not cached by default, so a high traffic read endpoint modelled as POST wastes infrastructure.
• A hidden _method field is only a convention. If the server framework does not enable the filter, the request stays a POST.
• Method alone is not security. GET versus POST does not stop CSRF. Only a token plus SameSite cookies do.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 5: too many filters for a URL

Branches

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• E commerce listing: GET with cache headers served from a CDN, giving millisecond responses for popular filter combinations.
• UPI or card payment: POST with an idempotency key, followed by a 303 redirect to a status page so refresh is harmless.
• Enterprise report builder: POST the filter definition, receive a saved search id, then GET /reports/ID which is shareable and cacheable.
• REST admin console: hidden _method fields to reach PUT and DELETE handlers when the page must work without JavaScript.
• Regulatory audit: PAN and Aadhaar always posted in a body, never as query parameters, so access logs stay clean.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 6: POST then redirect, with idempotency

Advanced Point 6: cacheable GET search

beginner.content:
1. Definition

• The enctype attribute tells the browser how to package the form data before sending it. It only matters when method is post.
• Three values exist:
• application/x-www-form-urlencoded is the default. Fields become name=value pairs joined by &.
• multipart/form-data splits the data into parts and is the only way to upload files.
• text/plain sends raw text and should be used only for debugging.

2. Purpose of This Topic

• To make file uploads actually work. Without multipart the server receives only the file name, not the file.
• To understand the shape of the request body so you can debug it in the network tab.

3. Need of This Topic

• Photo, signature and marksheet uploads are compulsory in Indian admission and KYC forms.
• The most common beginner bug is a file input inside a form that has no enctype.
• Knowing the encoding also explains why special characters like plus and space are escaped.
codeExamples:
Point 1 and 3: WRONG, file input without multipart

RIGHT: Point 2, multipart carries the real bytes

Point 1: default encoding, no file

beginner.content:
4. Advantages

• Multipart supports binary data, so images, PDFs and videos travel safely.
• Each part carries its own metadata such as the file name and content type, which helps the server validate.
• Urlencoded is compact and is what every server framework parses by default, so simple forms stay simple.
• You can mix normal text fields and files in one multipart request.

5. Disadvantages

• Multipart adds boundary text around every field, so it is heavier for a form that has no file.
• Uploads through a plain form give no progress bar and no cancel button.
• Servers set an upload size limit, and crossing it produces a confusing 413 error rather than a nice message.
• text/plain is not parsed reliably by servers and must not be used in production.
codeExamples: Point 5: guard the size before the server rejects it

beginner.content:
6. Real Time Examples

• College admission portal: photo, signature and 10th marksheet uploaded with multipart/form-data.
• Bank KYC: Aadhaar and PAN scans uploaded as multipart, each limited to a few hundred kilobytes.
• Naukri or LinkedIn: resume PDF upload.
• Passport Seva appointment: supporting documents uploaded in one multipart request along with the applicant details.
• Simple contact form on a college website: plain urlencoded, because there is no file.
• Instagram or WhatsApp Web: image upload built on the same multipart encoding, driven by JavaScript.
codeExamples:
Point 6: real admission upload page

Student details
Documents

expert.content:
1. Definition (Advanced)

• multipart/form-data builds a body where every entry is separated by a generated boundary string, and each part has its own Content-Disposition header carrying the field name and, for files, the filename.
• The browser chooses the boundary. You must never set the Content-Type header yourself when posting a FormData object with fetch, because you would destroy the boundary.
• urlencoded percent encodes reserved characters and turns spaces into plus signs, which is why a raw plus sign must be encoded as %2B.

2. Purpose of This Topic (Advanced)

• To design upload pipelines that stream to storage instead of buffering whole files in memory.
• To validate uploads by real content, not by the file extension the client claims.

3. Need of This Topic (Advanced)

• Security. The filename and the content type in a multipart part are attacker controlled. A file named invoice.pdf can be a script.
• Unbounded uploads are a denial of service vector, so size limits, part count limits and timeouts are mandatory.
• Storing an uploaded file inside the web root can lead to remote code execution. Store outside the web root or in object storage.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 1: what the browser actually sends

POST /kyc/upload HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryXyZ

------WebKitFormBoundaryXyZ
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="pan"

ABCDE1234F
------WebKitFormBoundaryXyZ
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="doc"; filename="aadhaar.jpg"
Content-Type: image/jpeg

(binary bytes)
------WebKitFormBoundaryXyZ--

expert.content:
4. Advantages (Advanced)

• Streaming friendly. Server libraries can pipe each part straight to disk or to S3 without loading it into memory.
• Per part metadata lets you reject a part early, before reading its whole body.
• FormData parity. The same object works for a native submit and for a fetch upload with a progress bar.
• Presigned uploads. You can skip your own server completely and let the browser post directly to cloud storage.

5. Disadvantages (Advanced)

• Multipart parsing bugs have caused serious vulnerabilities in the past, so keep the parser library patched.
• Boundary overhead makes multipart a poor choice for a JSON style API. Prefer application/json for pure data.
• Large uploads over an unreliable Indian mobile network need chunking or resumable uploads, which plain multipart does not offer.
• Antivirus scanning and image re-encoding add latency that must be handled asynchronously.
codeExamples:
Advanced Point 4: progress bar over the same multipart form

0 percent

expert.content:
6. Real Time Examples (Advanced)

• Aadhaar or PAN document capture: multipart to an internal service that verifies the magic bytes, strips EXIF data and stores the file in object storage under a random name.
• Job portal resume upload: XMLHttpRequest progress on the same multipart form so users on 4G see feedback.
• Presigned direct upload: the server issues a signed URL and the browser posts the file straight to cloud storage, keeping the application servers free.
• Insurance claim portal: ten photographs uploaded in one multipart request with a part count limit to avoid abuse.
• Global SaaS import: a CSV posted as multipart while all other endpoints use application/json, showing that enctype is chosen per endpoint.
codeExamples: Advanced Point 6: claim photos with client and server guards

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The autocomplete attribute tells the browser whether and how it may fill in a field automatically.
• It can be set on a form or on single inputs.
• The value on is the default and off asks the browser not to suggest values.
• Specific tokens such as email or postal-code say what the field holds.

Key Points

• Tokens include name, email, tel, street-address, postal-code and cc-number.
• Password fields use current-password or new-password.
• One-time codes use one-time-code so phones can paste an SMS code.
• Correct tokens save users a lot of typing on mobile.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>autocomplete</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="n">Full name</label>
  <input id="n" name="name" autocomplete="name">
  <label for="e">Email</label>
  <input id="e" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
</form>
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use autocomplete="new-password" on sign-up so password managers offer to generate one.
• Use autocomplete="current-password" on login forms.
• Prefix a token with a group such as shipping or billing to separate address blocks.
• Set autocomplete="off" only for sensitive or one-off fields such as a search of private data.

Common Mistakes

• Using off everywhere, which blocks password managers and annoys users.
• Using wrong tokens, so the browser fills the wrong data.
• Forgetting the name or id of the field, which browsers also use to guess.
• Expecting autocomplete="off" to be honoured by every browser on login fields.

Try It Yourself

• Make a sign-up form with name, email, new-password and postal-code fields using the correct tokens, then try it with your browser saved data.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>address tokens</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="a">Shipping address</label>
  <input id="a" name="ship" autocomplete="shipping street-address">
  <label for="z">Postal code</label>
  <input id="z" name="zip" autocomplete="shipping postal-code">
  <label for="c">One-time code</label>
  <input id="c" name="otp" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code">
</form>
</body>
</html>

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Checkout forms rely on correct tokens to complete in seconds on mobile.
• Sign-in pages use current-password and username so managers fill both fields.
• Accessibility guidelines (WCAG 1.3.5) require suitable autocomplete values for personal data fields.
• Banks use one-time-code to read SMS codes automatically on supported phones.

Best Practices

• Use the standard tokens from the HTML specification.
• Test forms with a password manager and a phone.
• Do not disable autocomplete unless there is a real reason.
• Keep field names meaningful as a second hint.

Interview Question

• Q: Why is autocomplete important for accessibility?
• A: It helps people with motor or cognitive difficulties by letting the browser fill in personal data, and WCAG requires correct tokens for fields that collect it.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>signup</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="u">Email</label>
  <input id="u" type="email" name="username" autocomplete="username">
  <label for="p">Choose a password</label>
  <input id="p" type="password" name="password" autocomplete="new-password">
</form>
</body>
</html>

beginner.content:
What It Is

• The input element creates an interactive field where the user enters data.
• It is a void element, so it has no closing tag.
• The type attribute chooses what kind of control appears.
• The default type is text.

Key Points

• Important attributes: name, value, type, id and placeholder.
• name is the key sent to the server with the value.
• Pair every input with a label for accessibility.
• More than twenty types exist, from text to colour and file.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>input</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="q">Your name</label>
  <input id="q" name="name" type="text" value="Asha">
  <button>Send</button>
</form>
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Browsers validate types such as email, url and number on submit.
• Use required, min, max and pattern to add rules without JavaScript.
• Read values in script with input.value and listen to the input event for live changes.
• Unsupported types fall back to text, so the form still works.

Common Mistakes

• Forgetting the name attribute, so the value is not submitted.
• Using the placeholder as the only label.
• Setting the type after the page has loaded and expecting all browsers to react.
• Using a text input where a more specific type would give a better mobile keyboard.

Try It Yourself

• Create a form with a text, email and number input, each with a label. Submit it and look at the query string to see how the names become keys.
codeExamples: You typed:

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Search boxes, login forms and filters are all built from input elements.
• Frameworks wrap input in controlled components that keep value and state in sync.
• Mobile keyboards change with type and inputmode, which improves speed.
• Custom styled inputs must keep focus outlines and labels.

Best Practices

• Choose the most specific type available.
• Always connect a label, using for and id.
• Validate on the server as well as in the browser.
• Keep names unique and consistent with your backend.

Interview Question

• Q: Which attribute decides what data is sent for an input?
• A: The name attribute is the key and the current value is the data, so a field without a name is never submitted.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>types</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <input type="email" name="e" placeholder="Email">
  <input type="number" name="n" min="1" max="10" placeholder="1-10">
  <input type="date" name="d">
  <input type="color" name="c" value="#ea580c">
</form>
</body>
</html>

beginner.content:
What It Is

• type="text" creates a single line text field.
• It is the default type, used for names, titles and short answers.
• The browser removes line breaks from what the user pastes.
• The value is always a string.

Key Points

• Use placeholder for a short hint, never as the only label.
• Use maxlength and minlength to limit the length.
• Use size for a rough visible width, or CSS width for exact control.
• Add readonly or disabled to stop editing.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>text input</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<label for="n">First name</label>
<input type="text" id="n" name="first" placeholder="e.g. Asha" maxlength="30">
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• pattern applies a regular expression, for example letters only.
• Use autocomplete tokens such as given-name to help the browser.
• spellcheck="false" suits usernames and codes.
• inputmode changes the mobile keyboard without changing validation.

Common Mistakes

• Using type text for numbers, emails or dates, which loses validation and keyboards.
• Using only a placeholder instead of a label.
• Trimming the value only on the client. Trim on the server too.
• Setting maxlength too small for real names.

Try It Yourself

• Build a username field that accepts three to twelve letters or digits, shows the rules in a title and displays remaining characters as you type.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>pattern</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="u">Username (letters and digits, 3-12)</label>
  <input id="u" name="u" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9]{3,12}" title="3 to 12 letters or digits" required>
  <button>Check</button>
</form>
</body>
</html>

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Usernames, titles and search terms rely on text inputs.
• Counters show remaining characters with a small script.
• Names should allow spaces, accents and long values.
• Frameworks use controlled text inputs with value and onChange.

Best Practices

• Be generous with lengths and characters for names.
• Show the rules near the field, not only in an error.
• Do not block paste on text fields.
• Test with long and non-English text.

Interview Question

• Q: Why is the placeholder not a replacement for a label?
• A: It disappears as soon as the user types, has low contrast and is not reliably announced by screen readers. A label stays visible and is linked to the field.
codeExamples: 40 left

beginner.content:
What It Is

• type="password" hides what the user types behind dots or bullets.
• It protects against people looking over a shoulder.
• It does not encrypt anything. The value is still sent as plain text unless you use HTTPS.
• Browsers and password managers recognise it and offer to save or fill it.

Key Points

• Use autocomplete="current-password" on login forms.
• Use autocomplete="new-password" on sign-up and change forms.
• Add minlength to enforce a minimum size.
• Never put a real password in a value attribute.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>password</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="p">Password</label>
  <input type="password" id="p" name="password" minlength="8" autocomplete="current-password" required>
</form>
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• A show-password toggle switches the type between password and text with a button.
• Allow paste so users can use password managers.
• Show requirements next to the field and update them as the user types.
• Always send forms with passwords over HTTPS and use POST.

Common Mistakes

• Blocking paste, which pushes users to weak passwords.
• Setting autocomplete off, which breaks managers.
• Limiting passwords to a short maximum length or a narrow set of symbols.
• Sending passwords with GET, which exposes them in URLs and logs.

Try It Yourself

• Create a sign-up password field with a show and hide button and a live rule that turns green after eight characters.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>toggle</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<label for="p">Password</label>
<input type="password" id="p" autocomplete="new-password">
<button type="button" id="b" aria-pressed="false">Show</button>
<script>
  b.onclick = () => {
    const show = p.type === 'password';
    p.type = show ? 'text' : 'password';
    b.textContent = show ? 'Hide' : 'Show';
    b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', show);
  };
</script>
</body>
</html>

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Every login and sign-up page has a password field.
• Strength meters guide users but must not replace server checks.
• Two-factor flows add a one-time-code field after the password.
• Security audits check that passwords never appear in URLs or logs.

Best Practices

• Hash passwords on the server with a modern algorithm.
• Prefer long passphrases to complex rules.
• Support password managers and passkeys.
• Rate limit login attempts.

Interview Question

• Q: Does type="password" make the form secure?
• A: No. It only masks the characters on screen. Security depends on HTTPS, a POST request, server-side hashing and rate limiting.
codeExamples: • At least 8 characters

beginner.content:
What It Is

• type="email" is a field for an email address.
• The browser checks the value has a simple address shape such as name@domain.
• Mobile keyboards show the @ and dot keys.
• With multiple it accepts a comma separated list.

Key Points

• Validation happens when the form is submitted.
• The check is loose: a@b passes, because it is a valid local address.
• Whitespace around the value is trimmed automatically.
• Use required to make it mandatory.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>email</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="e">Email</label>
  <input type="email" id="e" name="email" placeholder="you@example.com" required>
  <button>Subscribe</button>
</form>
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Add pattern for a stricter rule, such as a company domain.
• Use autocomplete="email" to let the browser fill it in.
• Use :invalid and :valid in CSS to style the state.
• Read input.validity.typeMismatch for custom messages.

Common Mistakes

• Relying only on browser validation. The server must verify the address too, ideally with a confirmation mail.
• Writing complicated regular expressions that reject real addresses.
• Showing errors before the user has finished typing.
• Using type text, which lacks validation and the right keyboard.

Try It Yourself

• Create an email field that is required, styles itself red while invalid and shows a custom error message in your own words.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>multiple</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
  input:invalid { border-color: crimson; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <label for="m">Invite friends (comma separated)</label>
  <input type="email" id="m" multiple placeholder="a@x.com, b@y.com">
  <button>Invite</button>
</form>
</body>
</html>

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Newsletter sign-ups, logins and contact forms all use it.
• Verification links prove the address belongs to the user.
• Typos in domains are caught with suggestions such as gmial.com to gmail.com.
• Privacy rules require consent and a way to unsubscribe.

Best Practices

• Be lenient in the browser and strict on the server through verification.
• Normalise to lowercase before comparing.
• Show a clear error text next to the field.
• Never expose other people addresses in the markup.

Interview Question

• Q: Is browser email validation enough?
• A: No. It only checks the shape. The server must validate again, and a confirmation email is the only reliable proof that the address works.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>custom message</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <input type="email" id="e" required>
  <button>Go</button>
</form>
<script>
  e.oninvalid = () => e.setCustomValidity('Please enter a valid email like name@example.com');
  e.oninput = () => e.setCustomValidity('');
</script>
</body>
</html>

beginner.content:
What It Is

• type="number" is a field for numeric values.
• It shows small up and down arrows (spinners) in most browsers.
• Mobile devices show a numeric keyboard.
• The value is still a string in JavaScript, so convert it with Number().

Key Points

• min and max set the allowed range.
• step sets the increment, such as 1, 0.5 or any.
• The default step is 1, so decimals fail validation unless you set step.
• Scrolling the mouse wheel over a focused number field can change it by accident.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>number</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<label for="q">Quantity (1-10)</label>
<input type="number" id="q" name="qty" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="1">
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use step="0.01" for prices and step="any" for free decimals.
• Use inputmode="numeric" with a text input for codes such as PINs.
• Check valueAsNumber for a real number or NaN.
• Style the spinners away with CSS when they clutter the design.

Common Mistakes

• Using type number for phone numbers, card numbers or ZIP codes, which can lose leading zeros.
• Forgetting step for decimals so 2.5 is rejected.
• Expecting max to prevent typing a larger number. It only fails validation.
• Allowing the wheel to change values silently.

Try It Yourself

• Create a quantity field limited to 1-10, a price field with two decimals and a PIN field that uses a numeric keyboard but keeps leading zeros.
codeExamples: Doubled:

expert.content:
Real-World Use

• Shopping carts use number inputs for quantity.
• Forms for ages, heights and scores set tight ranges.
• For PINs and codes, text with inputmode numeric is the better choice.
• Locale differences, such as decimal commas, are handled by the browser.

Best Practices

• Pick number only for values you calculate with.
• Always provide min and max where they make sense.
• Show the unit next to the field.
• Validate the range on the server too.

Interview Question

• Q: Why not use type number for a phone number?
• A: Phone numbers are identifiers, not quantities. They may contain a plus sign, spaces or leading zeros that number inputs would drop or reject.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>pin</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<label for="pin">PIN code</label>
<input id="pin" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]{6}" maxlength="6" autocomplete="postal-code">
</body>
</html>

beginner.content:
What It Is

• type="tel" is a field for a telephone number.
• Phones show a dial pad keyboard.
• The browser does not validate the format, because numbers differ across countries.
• The value is plain text.

Key Points

• Use pattern to apply your own format rules.
• Use autocomplete="tel" so browsers fill in the saved number.
• Spaces, plus signs and dashes are allowed.
• A tel: link in the page makes numbers tappable.
codeExamples:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="UTF-8"><title>tel</title>
<style>
  body { font-family: sans-serif; }
  label { display: block; margin: 10px 0 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; padding: 6px 8px; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<label for="t">Mobile number</label>
<input type="tel" id="t" name="phone" autocomplete="tel" placeholder="+91 98765 43210">
</body>
</html>

intermediate.content:
In Practice

• Use a pattern for an expected country format such as ten digits.
• Show an example in the placeholder or the hint.
• Clean the value on the server by removing spaces and dashes.
• Consider a country selector with a library for international numbers.

Common Mistakes

• Applying a strict pattern that rejects valid international numbers.
• Using type number, which removes the plus sign and leading zeros.
• Not telling users which format you expect.
